Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent that runs on the person's own API key or on JusPrin's hosted gateway, an Obico-server endpoint live in production since 2026-10-25. The gateway is about to start charging in credits: a Standard message 1 credit, an Expert message 5; 500 credits in the first month; packs that never expire; Hobby $10 and Workshop $20 subscriptions. The design was reviewed by Kenneth on 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02 and is final at canvas version 71; his wording decisions are in the design doc and must be kept exactly ("Standard" not "Basic" for people, config value stays `basic`; prices always carry "a message"; "your first month", never "trial"; "Get more credits" is the one action outside the pricing page; a chat keeps its model after the person's first message; the app's own turns run on Expert, free, and do not fix the chat's model). The two working docs and the brief are untracked at the repo root on purpose: never commit them or hide them in ignore files. Several agent sessions build on this Mac at once: limit builds to -j4, check for running ninja first, one build per build directory. Production (app.obico.io) is live and must not be changed; staging is app-stg.obico.io; for gcloud or kubectl use the account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com, read-only on production. House rules in `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` apply, in particular tokens for every UI value and no edits outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` without the rebase evidence the stewardship doc asks for.

Task:
Build the JusPrin Cloud credits system and finish the first-run onboarding flow, following the brief in `credits-and-onboarding-handoff-2026-11.md` at the root of `~/Projects/JusPrin` (untracked; read it first and in full, then the two documents it names in section 2: `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` and `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md`, same folder, and the board captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/` with their `MANIFEST.md`).

Do the steps in the order the plan's section 11 gives them, in your own worktrees, never in the main checkouts:

0. Port the branch `onboarding-frontend-only` (one commit, `8f4588beae`) onto `jusprin-newui`. Expect conflicts in 18 of its 27 files (the brief's section 4 lists them and the Home commits that caused them); keep both sides' additions. Then bring its screens to the canvas's "On boarding experience" page and boards 1a to 1d: the first-month offer as the headline ("Your first month: 500 credits", "Sign in for 500 credits"), and every "Set up JusPrin" entry point opening Preferences › Agent instead of a web link. Show the two paths the branch never verified in the real app.
1. Gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch from `master`, your own worktree): the credit ledger and charging in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, the `slicer-basic` alias with image stripping, `GET /account`, the 402 body with `basic_only_credits`, with the pytest list in plan section 11 step 1.
2. App: prices in the pickers ("1 credit a message"), pickers greyed once the person has sent a message, app-started turns on the Expert alias without storing the chat's model, the attachment row's picture notice with "New Expert chat", picture tools left out of a Standard chat's tool list, the balance ring and hover panel, the pre-send check with "Get more credits" and the conditional "New Standard chat", the failed-message card. Leave out the webview that opens the Account and pricing pages.
4. The 1-hour cache ttl in `prepare()` and the slice-polling guard.
5. Print-report rewards: endpoint, storage, admin review, the Print history button and form, the Home card line.

Do not start step 3 (Chargebee, the Account and pricing pages, v1-subscriber carry-over): it waits on Kenneth's decisions 12 (pages served into a webview or built into the app), 10 (domain) and the open parts of 8, listed in plan section 12. Build the items that have a recommended or placeholder answer in the plan as written and flag them in your report; never settle an open decision yourself. Where a board, the design doc and the plan disagree, say so rather than pick.

Done means: every step above has its tests passing (Catch2, Vitest, gateway pytest), the real app has been exercised for what tests cannot cover, no live-model run has happened without Kenneth approving its batch and spend, nothing is committed until he asks, and your report has four parts under 500 words: the problem, what you built, what you tested and how, what remains, saying plainly what you did not verify.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_756f4482-e5c7-45b4-bc36-5e6db3b079ef
I'll start by reading the brief, the two documents it names, and the sibling notes.

1	# Handoff: build JusPrin Cloud credits and finish the first-run onboarding
2	
3	Written 2026-11-02 for a coding agent who has not seen the design sessions. This is a working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Kenneth tracks unfinished work by the untracked files in `git status`.
4	
5	## 1. What you are building, in one paragraph
6	
7	JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent. The agent can run on the person's own API key (free, no account) or on JusPrin's hosted gateway (an Obico-server endpoint, `app.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/…`, live in production since 2026-10-25). The gateway is about to start charging in credits: a Standard message costs 1 credit, an Expert message 5. People get 500 credits in their first month, can buy packs that never expire, or subscribe (Hobby $10, Workshop $20). This work adds the credit ledger and charging to the gateway, the balance, prices and pre-send checks to the app's composer, the Account and pricing pages, print-report rewards, and finishes the first-run onboarding flow that a month-old branch started. Nothing of this is built yet; the design is done and reviewed.
8	
9	## 2. Read these first, in this order
10	
11	1. `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` (same folder). The whole technical plan: ledger tables, the charging algorithm, the `/account` JSON, the 402 body, alias config, Chargebee, rewards, section 11 "Order of work and tests", section 12 "Decisions still Kenneth's". Build from it.
12	2. `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md`. Each point where a person meets credits, the five rules that apply everywhere, and the exact wording. When the plan and this doc disagree on words, this doc wins.
13	3. The boards. Captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/` (one PNG per board, `credits-<board>-<slug>.png`, `-dark` variants where they exist). `MANIFEST.md` there lists every board with its canvas page and name; `CHANGELOG-v54-to-v69.md` records why each board looks the way it does. The live canvas is the JusPrin v2 design artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, at version 71. Figma is retired; do not design from it.
14	4. `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `fork-stewardship.md`, `design-system.md`. House rules; the ones that bite most often are repeated in section 7 below.
15	
16	## 3. Where the code lives
17	
18	You run on Kenneth's Mac, the machine the design sessions ran on, so every path below is live. The three repositories are checked out here and on GitHub: the app at `~/Projects/JusPrin` (`git@github.com:TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin.git`, branch `jusprin-newui`), the gateway at `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (`git@github.com:kennethjiang/tsd-enterprise.git`, branch `master`, with `obico-server` as a submodule), and deployment at `~/Projects/ops` (`git@github.com:kennethjiang/ops.git`). Other agent sessions work in these checkouts at the same time: make your own worktree for each repository you change, never reuse one you did not create, and touch nothing in the main checkouts themselves. The working docs this brief names sit untracked at the root of `~/Projects/JusPrin`; read them from there and leave them where they are.
19	
20	**App (this repository).** Branch `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4`, in sync with `origin`. Work in your own worktree and branch; never reuse another session's worktree.
21	- Composer, pickers, attachments, Preferences page: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/` (`Composer.tsx`, `ModelPickers.tsx`, `AttachmentChip.tsx`, `Preferences.tsx`, `WelcomeBack.tsx`).
22	- Host side of the agent: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` (`AgentHost.cpp` holds `chat_model_choice`, `use_chat_model`, `start_turn`; `ProviderAgent` sends the gateway headers and maps HTTP errors; `CloudAccount.cpp` and `ModelCatalog.cpp` hold the account's model list).
23	- Home page and onboarding: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` and `HomeUI/src/`. Preferences window: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/`. The v1 import and the welcome-back window: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/V1Import/`.
24	- Tests: Catch2 under `tests/jusprin/` and `tests/brand/`; Vitest beside each TypeScript file; the shell harness under `tests/shell/` drives the built app without a screen.
25	- Build: `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all -- -j4`. The Mac is shared by several agent sessions: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, one build per build directory, never restart a running build. Editing a CMake file rebuilds everything.
26	
27	**Gateway (tsd-enterprise).** Repository `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch from `master` (it moved 12 commits past the gateway merge, including the Python 3.12 / Django 5.2 bump), in your own worktree. The gateway is `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` (`aliases.py`, `upstream.py`, `gateway.py`, `stream.py`, `credits.py`, `auth.py`, `errors.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`; tests in `tests/test_gateway.py` and `tests/test_aliases.py`, using the MockTransport injection the file already uses). `obico-server` is a git submodule: never stage or commit a submodule change. The local stack from the previous session is compose project `jusprin-cloud` on port 3434 (`docker-compose.local-ports.yml` in `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/jusprin-cloud`, whose `LOCAL_TEST_ACCOUNT.txt` holds a test account), with `web_ent/scripts/jusprin/fake_upstream.py --port 8765` standing in for the model vendor. The session cookie is scoped to `.localhost`, so pass it as a header from scripts.
28	
29	**Deployment (ops).** `~/Projects/ops`: the alias ConfigMap is `tsd/prod/jusprin-v2-gateway.yaml` and `tsd/stg/jusprin-v2-gateway.yaml`. Staging is `https://app-stg.obico.io` and runs the same image as production. Production is live for real users: do not change it. For any `gcloud` or `kubectl` command, first run `gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, and stay read-only on production.
30	
31	## 4. Step 0: the onboarding branch
32	
33	`onboarding-frontend-only` (one commit, `8f4588beae`, Kenneth, 2026-10-06; `origin/onboarding-frontend-only` is identical) adds the local first-run path to Home: welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or choose a printer setup, open a project or the bundled example. Its commit message is a good spec of what it does and what it deliberately left out. It is 139 commits behind `jusprin-newui`.
34	
35	A dry-run rebase on 2026-11-02 conflicted in 18 of its 27 files. Expect to resolve `HomeBackend.hpp`, `HomeHost.cpp`, `HomeHost.hpp`, `HomeSnapshot.hpp`, `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`, `OrcaHomeBackend.hpp`, `resources/jusprin/home/protocol.json`, `HomeUI/src/App.tsx`, `App.test.tsx`, `bridge/protocol.ts`, `bridge/protocol.test.ts`, `state/store.ts`, `styles.css`, `styles.test.ts`, `tokens.ts`, `sources.cmake`, `tests/jusprin/test_home_host.cpp` and `test_home_snapshot.cpp`. Nine files apply cleanly, among them the three new ones (`OnboardingModel.cpp/.hpp`, `Onboarding.tsx`, `test_onboarding_model.cpp`). What changed underneath: the Home v3 page (`dbec3e3a38`), Print history (`ebbb2f8894`), JusPrin's own Preferences window (`641c17f13e`), every opened file becomes a new project (`d921c4b3dd`), the token sync (`7671e48504`). Most conflicts should be two additive hunks in the same place; keep both.
36	
37	After the rebase, bring the flow to the current design:
38	- The canvas's "On boarding experience" page is the source of truth. The branch followed Figma frames; check each of its eight screens against the canvas before trusting its layout.
39	- Boards 1a to 1d add the first-month offer as the headline on its own surface: "Your first month: 500 credits", under it "That is 500 Standard or 100 Expert messages. Your own API key stays free.", button "Sign in for 500 credits", "Explore first" below. 1a is the setup row in Preferences › Agent over a first-run Home, 1b the welcome screen, 1c the welcome-back window the app already builds for a returning v1 user (signing in is the primary button there), 1d that window once a v1 subscriber has signed in. Never the word "trial"; no dollar figure.
40	- The branch's "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" links to jusprin.com/account go away: since 2026-10-23 every entry point to agent setup opens Preferences › Agent.
41	- The branch left two paths unverified in the real app: a preset import that leaves some presets behind, and staying on Home when the bundled example fails to open. Show both before calling the step done.
42	
43	## 5. Then the credits work, in the plan's order
44	
45	Section 11 of the plan has the steps and their tests. Summary of what each needs and what it waits on:
46	
47	| Step | What | Waits on |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| 1 | Gateway ledger and charging, the `slicer-basic` alias with image stripping, `/account`, the 402 body | Nothing. Start here on the server side. |
50	| 2 | App: prices in the pickers, pickers greyed after the person's first message, app-started turns on Expert without fixing the chat's model, the attachment row's picture notice, the ring and hover panel, the pre-send check, the failed card | Step 1's `/account` and 402 shapes, which the plan fixes already. The webview that opens Account and pricing waits with step 3. |
51	| 3 | Chargebee plans, add-ons, coupon, webhooks; the Account and pricing pages; v1-subscriber carry-over | Kenneth's decisions 12 (pages served into a webview, or built in the app), 10 (domain) and the open parts of 8 (when v1 subscribers move, how to word it). Do not start the pages until he has answered. |
52	| 4 | Cache ttl and the slice-polling guard | Nothing. |
53	| 5 | Print-report rewards: endpoint, storage, admin review, the Print history button and form, the Home card line | Nothing; Print history exists on `jusprin-newui`. |
54	| 6 | Savings alert, auto-reload, launch bonus | Steps 1 and 3. |
55	
56	Steps 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5 can be built now. Steps 1 and 2 can run in parallel in different repositories.
57	
58	## 6. Decisions you must not make yourself
59	
60	The plan's section 12 lists them. The ones with a recommended or placeholder answer written in the plan (default tier, alias ids, the 50-a-day cap, the 50-credit trickle, the 600 ceiling, the 25-credit reward, the launch discount form, bars and the ring's total, "New Standard chat", the picture in a new chat, the thinking picker on Standard) you build as written and flag in your report. The ones with no answer (webview or in-app pages, the domain, v1 move timing and wording, Pix) you leave alone and ask Kenneth. If a board, the design doc and the plan disagree, say so rather than picking.
61	
62	## 7. Rules that bite
63	
64	- **Words.** The cheap tier is "Standard" everywhere a person reads (the config value stays `basic`, the alias id `slicer-basic`, the flag `basic_only`). Prices always carry their unit: "1 credit a message", never "1 credit". "Your first month", never "trial". Only messages the person sends cost credits. "Get more credits" is the one action outside the pricing page. A file is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". Text the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards some of this; extend it when you add model-facing text.
65	- **Design tokens.** Every colour, radius, font and control size in UI code comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"). A value with no token gets a token and a guard first. The two-line tooltip on board 2c needs a design-system change, since tooltips are one line today.
66	- **OrcaSlicer-owned files.** Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching anything outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Changes there are small, additive, and come with the rebase evidence that document asks for.
67	- **Errors.** Do not catch what you cannot recover from; never turn an impossible state into a silent no-op; one generic error for rare failures. Section "Error handling discipline" in `AGENTS.md`.
68	- **Tests.** Every behaviour change gets a test, and the real app must be exercised for anything a test cannot cover. Reproduce a bug in the real app before fixing it; a failing fake is not a reproduction.
69	- **Model spend.** No live-model run (the shell harness against a real provider, the live prompt suite) without Kenneth approving that batch and its stated spend. The staging gateway at `app-stg.obico.io` counts.
70	- **Git.** Commit only when asked; never commit submodule pointers; no attribution lines in commits or PR descriptions; working docs like this one stay untracked.
71	
72	## 8. How you will know it works
73	
74	- Gateway: the pytest list in plan section 11 step 1, plus one end-to-end run through the local compose stack with `fake_upstream.py`: sign-up lot created on first contact, a Standard turn charges 1 from the expiring lot first, an Expert turn skips basic-only credits, the 402 body carries `basic_only_credits`, an app-origin turn charges 0.
75	- App: Vitest for `ModelPickers`, the new balance panel, the composer's disabled Send, the attachment row in a Standard chat; Catch2 for `ProviderAgent`'s headers and 402 handling and for an app-started turn leaving the chat's model unset until the person's first message; the Home and onboarding suites from the branch; one shell-harness run against staging at a spend Kenneth approves.
76	- Report in four parts, under 500 words: the problem, what you built, what you tested and how, what remains. Say plainly what you did not verify.

1	# JusPrin Cloud credits: implementation plan (working doc, 2026-11-01, order of work and readiness updated 2026-11-02)
2	
3	Untracked working document. It turns the pricing plan Kenneth settled on 2026-11-01 into concrete work on the three codebases involved: the gateway in `tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), the Obico server it is built on (`obico-server`, where the v1 credit table lives), and the desktop app (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and the Agent page under `AgentUI/`). Companion docs: `pricing-mental-model-2026-10.md`, `journey-cost-2026-10.md`, `obico-pro-pricing-data-2026-10.md`, `v1-pricing-data-2026-10.md`.
4	
5	Every "recommend" below is my opinion; every "decided" is Kenneth's. Code facts were read from the checkouts on 2026-11-01 (tsd-enterprise master, JusPrin `jusprin-newui` at 69780c7af4, ops master).
6	
7	## 1. The plan being implemented
8	
9	- The unit is a **credit**, about 2 cents (decided 2026-11-01: "credits", not the placeholder "coins"). Credits pay per message, not per token. A **Standard** message (DeepSeek V4 Flash class) costs 1 credit; an **Expert** message (Claude Sonnet 5.5 class, not Opus) costs 5 credits. The 1:5 ratio is decided. Wherever a balance is shown it is shown translated, "612 credits left. That is 612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", so nobody converts in their head; the Expert count leaves out basic-only credits (612 with 50 free Standard messages is (612 − 50) / 5 = 112).
10	- **Pay as you go** (the pack): 500 credits for $10, never expire. Optional auto-reload at a discount.
11	- **Hobby, $10 a month:** 750 credits, Standard messages cost credits, unused credits lost at the end of each month.
12	- **Workshop, $20 a month:** 1,000 credits plus unlimited Standard messages, unused credits lost each month. Needs fair-use wording.
13	- Plan names decided 2026-11-01: Hobby, Workshop, Pay as you go. No Pro, Plus or Premium, because Obico Pro exists next door.
14	- **Obico subscribers:** 20% off both subscriptions.
15	- **Your first month** (the sign-up grant, never called a trial): about $10 of credits (500), expiring after one month. **Trickle:** a free monthly Standard allowance for light users.
16	- **Rewards:** credits of real value for a print report with a photo and detailed text, with a human review flag for bad ones.
17	- **Launch period:** discounted, not free, credits.
18	- **Alert:** tell the person when their usage has grown to where a subscription saves them money.
19	- **BYOK** (the person's own API key) stays free with no sign-in.
20	
21	### The cost figures the margins rest on
22	
23	Measured per user message, one run per journey, from `journey-cost-2026-10.md` (Sonnet added 2026-11-01, so the peer session's "Sonnet still unmeasured" is out of date):
24	
25	| Tier | Model | Cost per user message | Price at 2¢ a credit | Gross margin |
26	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
27	| Standard | DeepSeek V4 Flash (OpenRouter) | 0.4¢ to 1¢; 5¢ when the agent polled the slicer 75 times | 2¢ (1 credit) | 50% to 80%; negative in the polling case |
28	| Expert | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 5.6¢ to 7.4¢, mean 6.3¢ over 14 messages | 10¢ (5 credits) | 26% to 44%, 37% at the mean |
29	| (not offered) | Claude Opus 5.5 | 10¢ to 21¢ | 10¢ | negative |
30	
31	"Per user message" divides a whole session's cost, including the turns the app starts by itself (file opened, slice finished), by the messages the person typed. So the margins above already assume app-started turns are not charged (see section 3.3). Two cost prerequisites move these: Anthropic's 5-minute cache expiry during a slow slice rewrote 72k tokens for $0.36 on Opus (section 7.1), and the slicer polling tripled one basic session (section 7.2).
32	
33	## 2. What exists today
34	
35	**Gateway.** `web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py` is a raw ASGI endpoint on daphne (`tsdws-prod`) that streams `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/messages` (Anthropic format) and `/responses` (OpenAI format) to an upstream model. `credits.py` admits each turn: a Redis rate limit of 60 turns a minute per person (`JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE`), then one v1 credit per turn through `consume_credit_for_pipeline` in `obico-server/backend/app/jusprin/ai_credits.py`, which decrements `JusPrinAICredit.ai_credit_used_current_month` against `ai_credit_free_monthly_quota` (50 a month, -1 for unlimited). A turn is every request that carries the same `X-JusPrin-Turn` header; title requests (`X-JusPrin-Request: title`) are free. The Redis keys `seen` and `charged` make the charge idempotent per turn for an hour. Exhaustion is a 402 with code `quota_exhausted`.
36	
37	**Aliases.** `aliases.py` reads `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` (a ConfigMap, `ops/tsd/prod/jusprin-v2-gateway.yaml`). Production has one alias, `slicer-1`, label "Slicer 1", efforts fast/thorough, Anthropic backend `claude-sonnet-5-5` at 100%, OpenAI backend `gpt-6.1-sol` at 0%. Only the formats `anthropic` and `responses` exist. There is no DeepSeek backend and no image stripping.
38	
39	**Account.** `GET /jusprin/api/me/` (obico-server `JusPrinMeViewSet`) answers `{"user": {...}, "ai_credits": {...}}`; the desktop app reads only the email (`CloudAccount.cpp:233`). `GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models` lists aliases with `format`, `efforts`, `default_effort`.
40	
41	**Billing.** Chargebee, site `obico`. v1 sells `jusprin-unlimited-monthly` ($6.99) and `jusprin-unlimited-annual` ($59.99) through `web_ent/jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py`: hosted checkout pages, a callback, a webhook that upserts `JusPrinPlan` and flips the v1 quota to -1. An Obico Pro discount coupon (30%) is applied at checkout after a live Chargebee status call. Obico's own code (`web_ent/app_ent/cb_views.py`, `detective_hour_accounting.py`) already has the two patterns the credit ledger needs: one-time packs sold as a non-recurring add-on on a placeholder subscription (`pre-paid-detective-hour-pack`, credited from the `invoice_generated` webhook, keyed `inv:<invoice id>`), and per-term included credits keyed `sub:<resource_version>:<suffix>` so a repeated webhook never double-credits. `DetectiveHourTransaction` is a ledger of signed amounts with a `forfeitable` flag; balance is a sum.
42	
43	**Obico subscriber check.** `app_ent.models.Subscription.active()` on `user.subscription`, mirrored to `user.is_pro`. Local, no Chargebee call needed.
44	
45	**Rewards precedent.** `credit_dh_for_contribution` (a Celery task) grants non-forfeitable detection hours for labelling print frames; `PrintShotFeedbackReview.invalid` is the per-label human review flag set in the admin.
46	
47	**Desktop app.** `ProviderProfile.hpp` row `jusprin` (default model `slicer-1`, `account_sign_in` true) makes `ProviderAgent` send `X-JusPrin-Turn`, `X-JusPrin-Request` (reply or title) and `X-JusPrin-Chat`. `ProviderAgent::http_error` maps 402 to `quota_exhausted` with the text "Your JusPrin account has used its Agent allowance for now. See your account for more." The Agent page gets `model_catalog` (per provider: models with `efforts`), `chat_model`, `account_status` (sign-in phase only) and `setup_keys` (the signed-in email). `ModelPickers.tsx` draws the per-chat model and effort pickers; `Preferences.tsx` has an `account` section. Print records (`ManufacturingHistory.hpp`, `GcodeRecord` with destinations and prints) live in the project file; nothing about them reaches the server.
48	
49	**Cache control.** `AnthropicCodec.cpp` sets `cache_control: {type: ephemeral}` with no `ttl` on the last tool, the system text and the last user message. The append-only chat record (commit 1635438d4f) already makes the slice-finished turn read the whole prior prompt from cache, so only expiry during a pause remains.
50	
51	**Slice polling.** `slice_start`'s result note already tells the model "Checking on it from this turn shows nothing the person can't already see" (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2155`). DeepSeek polled `workspace_inspect` anyway, 75 times in one run and twice in another.
52	
53	## 3. Gateway: the credit ledger
54

212	## 6. Fair use for unlimited basic
213	
214	Numbers: a basic message cost 0.4¢ to 1¢ normally and 5¢ when the agent polled the slicer, so Workshop loses money past 400 to 2,000 Standard messages a month after its 1,000 credits of expert are also used. Rule (recommend):
215	
216	- **Ceiling:** a monthly number of Standard messages at no credits; past it, a Standard message costs 1 credit from the balance like on Hobby. 600 is a placeholder chosen from the cost side alone: it caps the worst case at about $6 to $30 of cost on $20 of revenue. There is no engaged-usage source for how many Standard messages a heavy v2 person sends in a month; v1's heaviest payer at 130 chats a month is a floor from a product people had stopped using. Set the real ceiling from the first months of Workshop charge records.
217	- **Rate:** the existing 60 turns a minute, plus the 50 free app turns a day (3.3).
218	- **Automation:** the page says the plan is for a person using JusPrin, not for scripts or shared accounts; the ledger gives the numbers to act on, and acting is a human step through the admin, not a detector.
219	- **Page wording:** "Unlimited Standard messages for one person using JusPrin by hand; after 600 in a month, Standard messages cost 1 credit each. Expert messages always cost 5 credits." Say the number. Every surveyed vendor hides it and gets the anger at the boundary (mental model doc, question 2); whether 600 is a boundary almost nobody reaches is the thing the charge records will show, and a stated number can be raised without anyone noticing, where a hidden one cannot be defended.

221	The polling fix (7.2) is what makes the 5¢ case go away; until it ships, the ceiling is the only protection.

223	## 7. The two cost prerequisites
224	
225	### 7.1 Anthropic cache lifetime
226	
227	Fact: Sonnet 5.5 cache writes cost $2.50 per million tokens for the 5-minute lifetime and $4 for one hour (fetched 2026-11-01). A session wrote 40k to 80k tokens in all, so the 1-hour lifetime adds $0.06 to $0.12 per session; one expiry after a pause over 5 minutes rewrote 42k to 72k tokens, $0.10 to $0.18 at Sonnet rates. So the 1-hour lifetime pays for itself at one real pause per session, and a person who slices, waits, reads and types pauses more than that.
228	
229	Where (recommend): the gateway, not the app. `upstream.py`'s `prepare()` already parses the Anthropic body; it adds `"ttl": "1h"` to every `cache_control` block for the `anthropic` backend. 233	### 7.2 Stop the agent polling the slicer
234	
235	Two steps, the small one first:
236	
237	1. **Guard in the host** (`ToolExecutionCoordinator`): while a slice the agent started in this turn is running, a `workspace_inspect` that asks for `slicing`, or a `slice_report`, is answered with the tool error code `busy` and the message "The slice is still running. This turn has nothing left to do: the app starts a new turn with the outcome. Finish your reply." After the third such refusal in one turn the host ends the turn (the same path as the person's Stop) and the slice-finished note turn carries on. `busy` is in the one error-code list (`Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`), and a waiting slice is an expected state, so this is normal control flow, not a swallowed error. Each refused call still costs one small request, so three is the cap on the waste.
238	2. **End the turn at `slice_start`** (the real fix, later): when `slice_start` returns `started: true`, the host closes the turn instead of returning the result to the model, and the slice-finished note turn carries both the `tool_result` for that call and the note text in one user message. The model never gets a chance to poll, the person sees the model's text before the tool plus the slice card, and the follow-up request happens once. This touches `ProviderAgent`'s turn continuation and both codecs (a deferred tool result), so it is its own piece of work with the tool-pairing rules of both wire formats tested.
239	
240	The measured waste was two thirds of a basic session's cost on a debug build; a shipped build slices faster so the poll count is lower, but the fix removes the behaviour rather than the opportunity.

9	## Five rules that apply at every point (board 0)
10	
11	1. **One word, one unit, always translated.** "Credits" (decided 2026-11-01), never coins, never tokens. A credit is explained once, in messages: "an Expert message is 5 credits, a Standard message is 1". Every balance is shown translated, "612 credits left. That is 612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", so nobody converts in their head. The Expert count leaves out credits that only Standard can spend: 612 credits of which 50 are free Standard messages is (612 − 50) / 5 = 112, not 122 (the first boards said 122; fixed in canvas version 70). A price never stands alone: "1 credit" confused Kenneth on sight (2026-11-02), so it is always "1 credit a message", "5 credits a message". Dollars appear only on the page where money changes hands. Plans are Hobby ($10 a month), Workshop ($20 a month) and Pay as you go (the never-expiring pack); never Pro, Plus or Premium.
12	2. **Credits only move when the person sends a message.** Turns the app starts (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) are free, and the balance never changes without a message from the person. That one fact is what makes the balance trustworthy; it is stated on the pricing page in one sentence: "Only messages you send cost credits."

"Free Standard messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec." "Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire." Never a bare number that mixes them. The draw rule is stated once, in the breakdown: "Expiring credits are used first."

When the lot has expired, nothing says "you lost 388 credits"; the panel simply shows what remains. Losing something you did not pay for should not be dramatised.
63	
64	### 5. The next message costs more than the person has (boards 3a to 3d)
65	
66	Where: the composer, before sending; the failed-message card if the gateway refuses anyway.
67	
68	This is the boundary where every surveyed product earns its anger. Opinion, as drawn: catch it before sending. The app knows the balance and the chat's tier, so when the next Expert message cannot be paid, Send is disabled, one line above the composer says why, "You have 3 credits; this Expert chat needs 5 a message.", and the one action is "Get more credits" (3b). The typed text is untouched. Only a race between two sends reaches the gateway's 402; the failed card (3c) then shows the 402's words, "This message needs 5 credits; you have 3.", the same single action, and the message goes back into the composer.
69	
70	"New Standard chat" appears in one case only (3d): the person has free Standard messages left, which can pay for Standard but not for this Expert chat. The line reads "This Expert chat needs 5 credits a message. Your free Standard messages can only pay for Standard." with "Get more credits" and "New Standard chat"; the new chat opens on Standard with the typed text in its box and no earlier messages, so the earlier chat's context is lost (the design session's fill-in; Kenneth has not reviewed 3d, and if he drops New Standard chat altogether the board goes away). Under 5 credits there is no New Standard chat, because, as Kenneth put it, "if a user has <5 credits, no point for new basic chat here": it would run out within a few messages. Bought and plan credits pay for either tier, so only free Standard messages reach this case.
71	
72	Earlier than that (3a): when the balance falls below one session's worth of the chat's tier (about 25 credits for Expert, a placeholder from the four harness sessions of 3 to 6 messages, not from engaged usage), the composer says once "About 5 Expert messages left", so the boundary is expected, not met.
73	
74	### 6. Unlimited Standard and its ceiling (boards 4c, 5a)
75	
76	Where: the pricing page, Preferences › Account, one notice in the composer.
77	
78	Risk: "unlimited" that stops at a ceiling reads as a lie. Opinion: never write "unlimited" alone. The Workshop card says "Unlimited Standard messages for one person using JusPrin by hand, up to 600 a month; after that, 1 credit each." Account shows the ceiling as a bar like any other lot: "Free Standard messages · 188 of 600 left · Resets 1 Dec. After 600, Standard is 1 credit a message until then." A Standard message under the ceiling shows as 0 credits in the usage table. At 500, one notice. At 600, the picker's tooltip price changes to "1 credit a message" with one line saying why. The 600 is the plan's placeholder ceiling, set from cost, not from any engaged-usage source; whatever the number becomes, it is stated, because a stated number can be raised quietly and a hidden one cannot be defended.
79	
80	### 7. Subscription credits the person did not use (boards 7a to 7c)
81	
82	Where: above the composer once; Preferences › Account.
83	
84	Kenneth expects most subscribers to use under half their credits. Opinion: tell them. The month-end notice is the same as point 4. And the "a subscription would save you money" alert runs in both directions: when a subscriber has forfeited more than half their credits two months running, the alert says what Pay as you go would have cost instead (7c). That is the trust move Kenneth described, applied to the people it costs us something to tell; the measured Obico pattern is that resentment churn is the kind that never comes back.
85	
86	The alert itself (7a): one line above the composer, dismissable, "Hobby would have saved you $5.00 in the last 30 days.", with "See the sums" (7b opens the arithmetic) and "Subscribe". The sums must count the overrun: 820 credits in 30 days is $16.40 Pay as you go against $10 for Hobby plus 70 credits at 2¢ = $11.40, a saving of $5.00; 7b spells out "$11.40 on Hobby ($10 plus 70 more credits at 2¢ each)" (fixed in canvas version 70). It is on by default; its switch in Account reads "Alert me when a subscription would save me money. Once, above the message box. It also says when a plan isn't paying off."
87	
88	### 8. Buying (boards 5a, 5b)
89	
90	Where: the pricing page in the browser, then back in the app.
91	
92	Risk: the bounce to a browser, and the silence when the person returns ("did it go through?"). Opinion, as drawn: the page is headed "Credits and plans" with one sentence, "A Standard message is 1 credit and an Expert message is 5. Only messages you send cost credits.", and three cards: "Pay as you go · $10 once · 500 credits · These credits never expire · Buy 500 credits"; "Hobby · $10 a month · 750 credits a month · These credits reset each month. Unused ones don't carry over · Subscribe to Hobby"; "Workshop · $20 a month · 1,000 credits a month plus unlimited Standard (up to 600) · Subscribe to Workshop". Each card says the price in messages, "500 credits = 500 Standard or 100 Expert messages". Under the cards: "Everyone also gets 50 free Standard messages a month. Your own API key stays free and never uses credits." Launch double credits shows on the pack card with its end date. The Obico discount (5b) shows as the price itself, $8 and $16, with one line saying why and no coupon to type; Pay as you go keeps its price.
93	
94	Whether this page is served by the server into a webview in the app, or built into the app, is being decided (Kenneth raised it 2026-11-02; my recommendation is the server, see the plan's section 5.3). The boards do not change either way.
95	
96	Back in the app: the balance refreshes when the window regains focus, and the composer shows one line, "+500 credits", so the person knows it worked without opening Preferences.
97	
98	### 9. When the first month ends (boards 6a, 6b)
99	
100	Where: the first launch after day 30.
101	
102	Risk: the person comes back to zero and reads it as "the free trial is over, pay up", the moment Obico's data says people leave. Opinion, as drawn: a new chat starts on Standard and the composer says what is there, "50 free Standard messages this month". No wall, no modal, no notice about what expired, no "upgrade" word. Expert is one click away in the picker (6b) and shows its price. A chat already on Expert stays on Expert, because a chat keeps its model, so opening one shows board 3d.
103	
104	### 10. Rewards for a print report (boards 8a to 8d)
105	
106	Where: Print history, and the project card on Home.
107	
108	Opinion: show the reward before the work, in the button itself: "Tell us how it printed · 25 credits", on the Print history entry beside Print again and Export (8a), absent while printing, one report per G-code. Kenneth pointed at the print-history lesson of 2026-10-27, "don't assume users can easily go back to the original chat and find the card" and "when the print fails, the user is likely in a new chat already", so the chat's one-line G-code marker keeps its "history" link and gets no button. People come back to Home with the part in hand, so the offer is visible before they open Print history (8d): a project card gets the line when its latest G-code has finished and has no report, and it opens Print history filtered to that project; after two weeks the line goes away (the design session's guess at the limit, open). Export-only entries also get the button, because a print from USB never reports back; that sits oddly beside a Home card reading "Exported once · never printed" and is open too. The form (8b) opens from the entry and names it ("Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C"), says what earns the reward ("A photo of the printed object and a few sentences earn 25 credits."), takes the photo, the text and the person's own answer to "How did it come out?" (It worked / Partly / It didn't work), which is the report's outcome, not a print state: Print history stays without a failure state (decided 2026-10-27). Three rewarded reports a day; the form says so only when the person reaches it. Print history has no composer, so the confirmation is the entry's own row, "Report sent · 16:10 · 25 credits added" (8c), which says nothing about how the print went. If a report is later marked invalid, the clawback is a row in the Account usage table with a one-line reason, never a silent drop.
109	
110	### 11. Switching between own key and account
111	
112	Where: the model picker, which lists every provider the person set up.
113	
114	Opinion: credits and prices appear only on the JusPrin provider's entries. A person with both an own key and an account sees "OpenAI · gpt-5.4-mini" without a price and "JusPrin · Expert · 5 credits a message" with one. Nothing about credits appears anywhere for a person who never signs in, and there is no ring.
115	
116	### 12. Obico subscribers (boards 4c, 5b)
117	
118	Opinion: one line, shown as the price on the card and as a note in Account ("Obico Premium Subscriber: 20% off subscriptions"). It is detected, never claimed or entered. The wording is Kenneth's (board 5b: "Obico member -> Obico Premium Subscriber to make it more clear"). One note for him: Obico's own UI says "Pro plan" far more often than "Premium" (284 strings against 67 in tsd-enterprise, counted 2026-11-02; "AI Premium" is the Chargebee plan's internal name), so an Obico customer may know their plan as "Pro". His call; the boards stay as he asked unless he says otherwise.
119	
120	## Open for Kenneth
121	
122	- A picture staged in a new Standard chat, before the first message, when the picker still works: the same row with "New Expert chat", or just the sentence, since switching the picker is enough there. Not drawn.
123	- The thinking picker on the Standard tier: only on Expert (suggested) or on both.
124	- Default tier for a later new chat, after the first month: Standard (as drawn on 6a) or the last chosen.
125	- The reverse alert (subscription to Pay as you go) when a subscriber forfeits over half: on (my pick, drawn as 7c) or off.
126	- Bought credits with no bar (as drawn) or a bar; and what the composer's ring measures against.
127	- Whether "1 credit" was confusing for its missing unit (as the boards now read) or for the word "credit" itself.
128	- Pricing page and Account served by the server into a webview, or built into the app (plan section 5.4).
129	- v1 subscribers: the price holds "while subscribed"; 1,250 credits in the first month; the move at sign-in or at term end; how to say v1 was unlimited and Hobby is not.
130	- "New Standard chat" carrying only the typed text, and whether 3d stays.
131	- The Home card line's two-week limit, and the report button on export-only entries.
132	- Rule 5's wording on board 0 and rule 1's missing plan-names sentence there.
133	- What the balance panel calls reward credits, which never expire but are not bought (no board shows an unspent reward).
134	- A stray "Your text here" box on board 1a, hidden behind the Preferences window, from a page save of Kenneth's before version 64.
135	
136	Decided 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02, so no longer open: the unit is "credits"; prices always carry "a message"; the plans are Hobby, Workshop and Pay as you go; the sign-up grant is "your first month", never "trial"; every balance is shown translated; a chat keeps its model; the composer shows only a ring, the count is in the hover panel; a bar per kind of expiring credit; "Get more credits" is the one action outside the pricing page; "New Standard chat" never under 5 spendable credits; the offer is the headline on the sign-in screens and the button names the reward; "Your own API key"; v1 subscribers keep their original price on Hobby and get the 500; "Obico Premium Subscriber"; the report button lives in Print history, not the chat; boards live with their flows; the cheap tier is "Standard"; a picture in a Standard chat is dropped and the attachment row says so with a "New Expert chat" button (board 3e); app-started turns run on Expert, free, without fixing the chat's model.

=== jusprin-worktree-build
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata:

---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

=== check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

name: cmake-file-edit-forces-full-rebuild
description: "Editing sources.cmake (adding a file) after a commit re-runs CMake, which bakes the new HEAD into -DGIT_COMMIT_HASH on every compile line, so ninja rebuilds all ~970 steps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 62f57a5d-138a-485a-ac71-94d683a8c5db

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake` before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 6 18:47:26 2026 -0700

    Add the local first-run onboarding flow to Home
    
    A new user now gets a short guided path into a first project instead of
    landing on an empty Home screen. The path needs no account and no Agent:
    welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or
    choose a printer setup, then open a project or the bundled example.
    
    How it works
    - The native side decides which step is due. OnboardingModel is a pure
      function from saved progress plus three facts (user presets exist, a
      usable printer is selected, a project is open) to the next step.
      OrcaHomeBackend supplies the facts and stores progress in the app
      config under "jusprin_onboarding".
    - The Home page draws the step it is told to draw (Onboarding.tsx). The
      eight screens follow the Figma frames on the "On boarding experience"
      page; at 1280x800 the main block of each lands on its frame's
      rectangle.
    - The Home bridge stays on protocol version 1. The new state and
      messages are additive and announced through an "onboarding" entry in
      the capabilities list.
    
    What the page shows is what the app reported
    - The Figma frames carry sample data (an example source, example preset
      rows, a sample failure reason). None of it is repeated: preset names,
      counts, and the copied and not-copied lists come from the host, and a
      line the host cannot back is left out.
    - The three preset-kind checkboxes control what is imported, and
      "Review selection" lists the preset names found in the Orca folder.
    - A failed action is reported: on the project step as the recovery
      card, where Retry repeats the action that failed, and on other steps
      as a line above the buttons.
    
    Deliberately not built
    - Account and Agent setup. "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" are
      links that open jusprin.com/account.
    - The four dropdowns on the setup confirmation show the current value
      only; changing one goes through "Change or find printer".
    - Two sizes follow the token file where Figma differs: the close button
      is 26 px (Figma 32) and the breadcrumb chevron 16 px (Figma 14).
    
    Tokens: component.onboarding gains the frame widths (content 960, card
    480, example panel 472, setup field 220), guarded in
    test_brand_tokens.cpp. Home now also emits the checkbox, select, and
    form-row tokens as CSS variables.
    
    Verified: Home page tests (70), jusprin_tests (584 assertions), and
    brand_tokens_tests pass. Every screen was captured from the built app on
    isolated data folders and compared with Figma.
    
    Not verified end to end: a real import that leaves some presets behind
    (the partial-result screen was shown from a stored result), and the
    change that keeps the user on Home when the bundled example fails to
    open. The failure was reproduced before the change; the corrected
    behaviour was not demonstrated.

127	`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
128	`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
129	bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
130	still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
131	rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

134	runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
135	silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
136	success and compare binary mtime.

140	  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
141	  variable that shadows the cache.

143	  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive

162	=== check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
163	---
164	name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
165	description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
166	metadata:
167	  node_type: memory
168	  type: feedback
169	  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
170	  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
171	---
172	
173	On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.
174	
175	**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.
176	
177	**How to apply:**
178	- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
179	- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
180	- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
181	- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

The lesson, 2026-10-27: "don't assume users can easily go back to the original chat and find the card. where will users likely look when they are in each of these cases."
346	
347	**Why:** by the time a print is done the person is in a new chat or back hours later. Anything about one G-code belongs on that G-code's entry, the same reason Print again lives only there.
348	
349	**How to apply:** before placing an action in chat, ask where the person will be when they want it. Boards now: button on the entry (8a), form over Print history (8b), a "Report sent · 25 credits added" row instead of a composer line (8c), a line on the Home project card as the way there (8d). The Home line's rule and two-week limit, and the button on export-only entries, are my choices, asked in the thread. `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md` section 8 still says marker and composer. Related: [[print-history-screen-design]].

361	=== ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
362	---
363	name: ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
364	description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
365	metadata:
366	  node_type: memory
367	  type: project
368	  originSessionId: 33551592-d22c-4161-9a14-9a22ef798541
369	  modified: 2026-10-28T13:12:42.393Z
370	---
371	
372	On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).
373	
374	**Recipe that worked**
375	- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
376	- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
377	- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
378	- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
379	- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
380	- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.
381	
382	**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
383	**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
384	=== live-test-built-app-on-mac
385	---
386	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
387	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
388	metadata: 
389	  node_type: memory
390	  type: project
391	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
392	  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
393	---
394	
395	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
396	
397	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
398	
399	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
400	
401	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
402	
403	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
404	
405	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
406	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
407	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
408	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
409	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
410	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
411	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
412	the harness had opened on the Acer.
413	
414	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
415	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
416	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
417	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
418	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
419	
420	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
421	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
422	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
423	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
424	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
425	concluding anything about the app.
426	
427	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
428	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
429	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
430	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
431	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
432	
433	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
434	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
435	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
436	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
437	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
438	
439	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
440	
441	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
442	
443	**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
444	
445	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
446	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
447	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
448	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
449	had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
450	`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
451	all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
452	treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
453	`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
454	rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.
455	
456	**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
457	"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
458	reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
459	display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
460	sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
461	button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
462	until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
463	
464	**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).
465	
466	**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.
467	
468	**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.
469	=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
470	---
471	name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
472	description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
473	metadata: 
474	  node_type: memory
475	  type: feedback
476	  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
477	  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
478	---
479	
480	A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
481	bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
482	build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
483	which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
484	725-step JusPrin rebuild.
485	
486	**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
487	error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
488	compiled at all.
489	
490	**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
491	(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
492	then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
493	`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
494	[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
495	=== reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
496	---
497	name: reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
498	description: "A failing test with a fake backend is not a reproduction; run the pre-fix code against the real thing before fixing, and say what was and was not seen"
499	metadata:
500	  type: feedback
501	---
502	
503	A failing Catch2 test with a fake backend proves the code does what the brief says, not that the bug is real. Before fixing, run the code from before the fix against the real thing, with what the app actually knows printed beside what it says.
504	
505	**Why:** on 2026-11-01 Kenneth asked whether I had reproduced three printer chat bugs, and I had only fakes for them: "I don't want you to fix the bugs that are in imagination only". The real run then showed one was only partly real as briefed: the "No printer in LAN mode" sentence was true of a printer in cloud mode.
506	
507	**How to apply:** do it before writing the fix. To do it afterwards, swap production files with `git show <base>:<file>`, keep a temporary harness script, rebuild, and restore from `git show HEAD:<file>`. In zsh, loop over an array: a plain string variable does not split. Run harnesses with cwd in the scratchpad: the Bambu plug-in writes `log_iotc.txt` into the cwd. See [[printer-network-check-harness]].
508	=== prove-guard-tests-fail-first
509	---
510	name: prove-guard-tests-fail-first
511	description: A lint-style test that reads a source file must be shown failing on injected drift before it counts; Vitest hands CSS imports (even ?raw) back empty in the AgentUI setup.
512	metadata: 
513	  node_type: memory
514	  type: feedback
515	  originSessionId: 1b302f25-67a5-44d7-9f2c-02b68b2a0bb8
516	  modified: 2026-09-07T23:29:44.393Z
517	---
518	
519	In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.
520	
521	**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.
522	
523	**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

   I am a side session (started by session `local_756f4482-e5c7-45b4-bc36-5e6db3b079ef`; a single blocking question may go to it via `SendMessage`, load through ToolSearch). The task is to build the JusPrin Cloud credits system and finish first-run onboarding, following `credits-and-onboarding-handoff-2026-11.md`, `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md`, `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md` (untracked at root of `~/Projects/JusPrin`; re-read from there as needed) and board captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/` with `MANIFEST.md`. Steps, in plan section 11's order, in my own worktrees, never in the main checkouts:
   - **0.** Port `onboarding-frontend-only` (`8f4588beae`) onto `jusprin-newui`; keep both sides; bring screens to canvas "On boarding experience" page and boards 1a–1d: first-month offer as headline ("Your first month: 500 credits", "Sign in for 500 credits"), every "Set up JusPrin" entry point opens Preferences › Agent, not a web link. Show the two paths the branch never verified in the real app (a preset import leaving some presets behind; staying on Home when the bundled example fails to open).
   - **1.** Gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch from `master`, own worktree): credit ledger and charging in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` (plan says new module `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/`), `slicer-basic` alias with image stripping, `GET /account`, 402 body with `basic_only_credits`, pytest list in plan §11 step 1.
   - **2.** App: prices in pickers ("1 credit a message"), pickers greyed once person sent a message, app-started turns on Expert alias without storing chat's model, attachment row picture notice with "New Expert chat", picture tools left out of a Standard chat's tool list, balance ring and hover panel, pre-send check with "Get more credits" and conditional "New Standard chat", failed-message card.    - **4.** 1-hour cache ttl in `prepare()` and slice-polling guard.

Build items with a recommended/placeholder answer as written and flag them in report; never settle an open decision; where a board, the design doc and plan disagree, say so rather than pick (design doc wins on words over plan per brief).
