"""Per-turn admission: rate limit, then one credit per turn.

A turn is everything the client sends for one reply, including tool-call
follow-ups; every request of it carries the same X-JusPrin-Turn value. One turn
costs one credit, the v1 meaning of a credit, however many requests it makes.
Title requests are free.

The reply requests of one turn are sequential (a follow-up is built from the
previous answer), so the charge does not guard against two reply requests of
the same turn racing each other.
"""
import enum
import time

from django.conf import settings

from app.jusprin.ai_credits import consume_credit_for_pipeline
from lib.cache import REDIS

KEY_PREFIX = 'jusprin:v2'
TURN_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60


class Admission(enum.Enum):
    ADMITTED = 'admitted'
    RATE_LIMITED = 'rate_limited'
    QUOTA_EXHAUSTED = 'quota_exhausted'


def admit(user_id: int, turn_id: str, request_kind: str) -> Admission:
    """Count a new turn against the rate limit, then charge it once if it is a
    reply. Synchronous: Redis and the credit table are both blocking."""
    seen_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:seen:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if REDIS.set(seen_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        bucket = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:turns:{user_id}:{int(time.time() // 60)}'
        pipe = REDIS.pipeline()
        pipe.incr(bucket)
        pipe.expire(bucket, 120)
        turns_this_minute, _ = pipe.execute()
        if turns_this_minute > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE:
            # The turn was not admitted, so its retry is a new turn again.
            REDIS.delete(seen_key)
            return Admission.RATE_LIMITED

    if request_kind == 'title':
        return Admission.ADMITTED

    charged_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:charged:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if not REDIS.set(charged_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        return Admission.ADMITTED
    charged = False
    try:
        charged = consume_credit_for_pipeline(user_id)['success']
    finally:
        # Only a turn that actually paid is remembered as paid, whether the
        # quota ran out or the credit table raised.
        if not charged:
            REDIS.delete(charged_key)
    return Admission.ADMITTED if charged else Admission.QUOTA_EXHAUSTED
"""Model aliases for the JusPrin v2 gateway.

The client only ever sees an alias such as "slicer-1". What an alias means
upstream lives in the JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES setting, a JSON env var; nothing
about an upstream model is in code. Upstream keys stay in env vars that the
config names, never in the JSON itself.

Shape (every key shown is required unless marked optional; unknown keys are an
error so a typo fails at startup instead of silently changing routing):

    {
      "aliases": [                         # display order of the models endpoint
        {
          "id": "slicer-1",                # the only model id the client sees
          "label": "Slicer 1",
          "efforts": ["fast", "thorough"], # display order; may be empty
          "default_effort": "fast",        # one of efforts, or null when efforts is empty
          "backends": {                    # keyed by wire format, at least one of:
            "anthropic": {                 #   POST <base_url>/messages, Anthropic Messages API
              "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"},  # must cover every effort
              "headers": {"anthropic-version": "2023-06-01"}      # optional, extra request headers
            },
            "responses": {                 #   POST <base_url>/responses, OpenAI Responses API
              "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_OPENAI_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"}
            }
          },
          "groups": [                      # A/B assignment, percents sum to 100
            {"name": "anthropic-main", "format": "anthropic", "percent": 90},
            {"name": "responses-trial", "format": "responses", "percent": 10}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }

A person's group for an alias is fixed by a hash of their user id and the alias
id into one of 100 buckets; groups take consecutive buckets in listed order.
The group decides the "format" the models endpoint reports. It does not decide
where a request goes: the client pins a chat to the format it first saw, so the
endpoint a request arrives on picks the backend.
"""
import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Dict, Optional, Tuple

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured

FORMATS = ('anthropic', 'responses')


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Backend:
    format: str
    base_url: str
    model: str
    api_key_env: str
    effort_map: Dict[str, str]
    headers: Dict[str, str]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Group:
    name: str
    format: str
    percent: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Alias:
    id: str
    label: str
    efforts: Tuple[str, ...]
    default_effort: Optional[str]
    backends: Dict[str, Backend]
    groups: Tuple[Group, ...]

    def group_for(self, user_id: int) -> Group:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(f'{user_id}:{self.id}'.encode()).hexdigest()
        bucket = int(digest[:8], 16) % 100
        upper = 0
        for group in self.groups:
            upper += group.percent
            if bucket < upper:
                return group
        raise AssertionError('groups are validated to cover all 100 buckets')


def get_aliases() -> Dict[str, Alias]:
    """The configured aliases, in display order, keyed by id."""
    return parse_aliases(settings.JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES)


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def parse_aliases(raw: str) -> Dict[str, Alias]:
    if not raw.strip():
        return {}
    try:
        config = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES is not valid JSON: {e}') from e
    _keys(config, 'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES', {'aliases'})
    aliases = {}
    for entry in _typed(config['aliases'], list, 'aliases'):
        alias = _parse_alias(entry)
        if alias.id in aliases:
            raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: duplicate alias "{alias.id}"')
        aliases[alias.id] = alias
    return aliases


def _parse_alias(entry) -> Alias:
    _keys(entry, 'alias', {'id', 'label', 'efforts', 'default_effort', 'backends', 'groups'})
    alias_id = _typed(entry['id'], str, 'alias id')
    where = f'alias "{alias_id}"'
    efforts = tuple(_typed(e, str, f'{where} effort') for e in _typed(entry['efforts'], list, f'{where} efforts'))
    default_effort = entry['default_effort']
    if (default_effort is None) != (not efforts) or (default_effort is not None and default_effort not in efforts):
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} default_effort must be one of its efforts')

    backends = {}
    for fmt, spec in _typed(entry['backends'], dict, f'{where} backends').items():
        if fmt not in FORMATS:
            raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} has unknown backend format "{fmt}"')
        backends[fmt] = _parse_backend(fmt, spec, efforts, f'{where} {fmt} backend')
    if not backends:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} has no backend')

    groups = []
    for spec in _typed(entry['groups'], list, f'{where} groups'):
        _keys(spec, f'{where} group', {'name', 'format', 'percent'})
        group = Group(
            name=_typed(spec['name'], str, f'{where} group name'),
            format=_typed(spec['format'], str, f'{where} group format'),
            percent=_typed(spec['percent'], int, f'{where} group percent'),
        )
        if group.format not in backends:
            raise ImproperlyConfigured(
                f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} group "{group.name}" uses format "{group.format}" with no backend')
        if group.percent < 0:
            raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} group "{group.name}" has a negative percent')
        groups.append(group)
    if sum(g.percent for g in groups) != 100:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} group percents must sum to 100')

    return Alias(
        id=alias_id,
        label=_typed(entry['label'], str, f'{where} label'),
        efforts=efforts,
        default_effort=default_effort,
        backends=backends,
        groups=tuple(groups),
    )


def _parse_backend(fmt, spec, efforts, where) -> Backend:
    _keys(spec, where, {'base_url', 'model', 'api_key_env', 'effort_map'}, optional={'headers'})
    effort_map = _typed(spec['effort_map'], dict, f'{where} effort_map')
    missing = [e for e in efforts if not isinstance(effort_map.get(e), str)]
    if missing:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {where} effort_map does not map {missing}')
    headers = _typed(spec.get('headers', {}), dict, f'{where} headers')
    return Backend(
        format=fmt,
        base_url=_typed(spec['base_url'], str, f'{where} base_url').rstrip('/'),
        model=_typed(spec['model'], str, f'{where} model'),
        api_key_env=_typed(spec['api_key_env'], str, f'{where} api_key_env'),
        effort_map=dict(effort_map),
        headers={_typed(k, str, f'{where} header'): _typed(v, str, f'{where} header') for k, v in headers.items()},
    )


def _typed(value, kind, what):
    # bool is an int subclass; a percent of true is a config typo, not 1.
    if not isinstance(value, kind) or (kind is int and isinstance(value, bool)):
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {what} must be a {kind.__name__}')
    return value


def _keys(obj, what, required, optional=frozenset()):
    _typed(obj, dict, what)
    missing = required - obj.keys()
    unknown = obj.keys() - required - optional
    if missing or unknown:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(
            f'JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES: {what} is missing {sorted(missing)} or has unknown {sorted(unknown)}')
"""The gateway's own error answers.

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}} with text
from this table, never bytes from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed
out", so 401 means only that the person's own token was missing or rejected.
"""
import json

MESSAGES = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
    'unauthorized': 'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
    'quota_exhausted': 'Your JusPrin AI credits for this period are used up.',
    'request_too_large': 'The request is too large.',
    'rate_limited': 'Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.',
    'upstream_error': 'The model service could not answer.',
    'unavailable': 'The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly.',
    'timeout': 'The model service took too long to answer.',
    'busy': 'JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment.',
}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str = None):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]}}).encode()
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse
from django.shortcuts import render
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET

from .aliases import get_aliases
from .auth import authenticate
from .errors import error_body


@require_GET
def models(request):
    """The aliases this person can pick, in display order. "format" is the
    backend the person is currently assigned for the alias, and so the
    endpoint the client should use for a new chat."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    data = [{
        'id': alias.id,
        'label': alias.label,
        'format': alias.group_for(user.id).format,
        'efforts': list(alias.efforts),
        'default_effort': alias.default_effort,
    } for alias in get_aliases().values()]
    response = JsonResponse({'data': data})
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response

from oauth2_provider.oauth2_backends import get_oauthlib_core


def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    The same check DRF's OAuth2Authentication runs for the v1 JusPrin views: any
    valid token of the provider, whichever application issued it, no scope
    required. A deactivated account's token is refused as well.
    """
    valid, oauthlib_request = get_oauthlib_core().verify_request(request, scopes=[])
    if not valid or not oauthlib_request.user.is_active:
        return None
    return oauthlib_request.user

211	
212	## 6. Fair use for unlimited basic
213	
214	Numbers: a basic message cost 0.4¢ to 1¢ normally and 5¢ when the agent polled the slicer, so Workshop loses money past 400 to 2,000 Standard messages a month after its 1,000 credits of expert are also used. Rule (recommend):
215	
216	- **Ceiling:** a monthly number of Standard messages at no credits; past it, a Standard message costs 1 credit from the balance like on Hobby. 600 is a placeholder chosen from the cost side alone: it caps the worst case at about $6 to $30 of cost on $20 of revenue. There is no engaged-usage source for how many Standard messages a heavy v2 person sends in a month; v1's heaviest payer at 130 chats a month is a floor from a product people had stopped using. Set the real ceiling from the first months of Workshop charge records.
217	- **Rate:** the existing 60 turns a minute, plus the 50 free app turns a day (3.3).
218	- **Automation:** the page says the plan is for a person using JusPrin, not for scripts or shared accounts; the ledger gives the numbers to act on, and acting is a human step through the admin, not a detector.
219	- **Page wording:** "Unlimited Standard messages for one person using JusPrin by hand; after 600 in a month, Standard messages cost 1 credit each. Expert messages always cost 5 credits." Say the number. Every surveyed vendor hides it and gets the anger at the boundary (mental model doc, question 2); whether 600 is a boundary almost nobody reaches is the thing the charge records will show, and a stated number can be raised without anyone noticing, where a hidden one cannot be defended.
220	
221	The polling fix (7.2) is what makes the 5¢ case go away; until it ships, the ceiling is the only protection.
222	
223	## 7. The two cost prerequisites
224	
225	### 7.1 Anthropic cache lifetime
226	
227	Fact: Sonnet 5.5 cache writes cost $2.50 per million tokens for the 5-minute lifetime and $4 for one hour (fetched 2026-11-01). A session wrote 40k to 80k tokens in all, so the 1-hour lifetime adds $0.06 to $0.12 per session; one expiry after a pause over 5 minutes rewrote 42k to 72k tokens, $0.10 to $0.18 at Sonnet rates. So the 1-hour lifetime pays for itself at one real pause per session, and a person who slices, waits, reads and types pauses more than that.
228	
229	Where (recommend): the gateway, not the app. `upstream.py`'s `prepare()` already parses the Anthropic body; it adds `"ttl": "1h"` to every `cache_control` block for the `anthropic` backend. That keeps the pricing lever on the server, ships without an app release, and BYOK users keep paying Anthropic's default on their own key. Anthropic requires 1-hour breakpoints to come before 5-minute ones in the prompt; setting all three to 1h satisfies that. Verify on the live gateway by comparing `cache_creation_input_tokens` across a turn separated by a 10-minute pause, before and after.
230	
231	The slice-finished turn itself no longer rewrites the prefix since the append-only record landed (commit 1635438d4f); the 1-hour lifetime covers the slice taking longer than 5 minutes.
232	
233	### 7.2 Stop the agent polling the slicer
234	
235	Two steps, the small one first:
236	
237	1. **Guard in the host** (`ToolExecutionCoordinator`): while a slice the agent started in this turn is running, a `workspace_inspect` that asks for `slicing`, or a `slice_report`, is answered with the tool error code `busy` and the message "The slice is still running. This turn has nothing left to do: the app starts a new turn with the outcome. Finish your reply." After the third such refusal in one turn the host ends the turn (the same path as the person's Stop) and the slice-finished note turn carries on. `busy` is in the one error-code list (`Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`), and a waiting slice is an expected state, so this is normal control flow, not a swallowed error. Each refused call still costs one small request, so three is the cap on the waste.
238	2. **End the turn at `slice_start`** (the real fix, later): when `slice_start` returns `started: true`, the host closes the turn instead of returning the result to the model, and the slice-finished note turn carries both the `tool_result` for that call and the note text in one user message. The model never gets a chance to poll, the person sees the model's text before the tool plus the slice card, and the follow-up request happens once. This touches `ProviderAgent`'s turn continuation and both codecs (a deferred tool result), so it is its own piece of work with the tool-pairing rules of both wire formats tested.
239	
240	The measured waste was two thirds of a basic session's cost on a debug build; a shipped build slices faster so the poll count is lower, but the fix removes the behaviour rather than the opportunity.
241

def _scope_cache_key(fmt, body, user_id):
    """Puts the user id in front of the client's cache key. Every user shares
    the backend's one organisation, where OpenAI recommends a key per user to
    prevent cache-hit probing across users; a key the client sends cannot
    then land in another user's."""
    field = CACHE_KEY_FIELD.get(fmt)
    if field not in body:
        return
    key = body[field]
    if not isinstance(key, str) or key == '':
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', f'Field "{field}" must be a non-empty string.')
    body[field] = f'{user_id}:{key}'


def _headers(fmt, backend) -> Dict[str, str]:
    key = os.environ.get(backend.api_key_env)
    if not key:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'{backend.api_key_env}, the key for a JusPrin v2 {fmt} backend, is not set')
    auth = {'x-api-key': key} if fmt == 'anthropic' else {'authorization': f'Bearer {key}'}
    return {
        **backend.headers,
        **auth,
        'content-type': 'application/json',
        'accept': 'text/event-stream',
    }


def error_for_status(status: int) -> GatewayError:
    """The answer for an upstream non-200 status. Upstream 401/403 means the
    gateway's own key failed: a gateway fault (502), never the client's 401."""
    if status == 429:
        return GatewayError(429, 'rate_limited')
    if status in (400, 422):
        return GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The model service did not accept the request.')
    if status == 413:
        return GatewayError(413, 'request_too_large')
    if status >= 500:  # includes Anthropic's 529 overloaded
        return GatewayError(503, 'unavailable')
    return GatewayError(502, 'upstream_error')


def is_gateway_fault(status: int) -> bool:
    """Statuses that mean the gateway's configuration is wrong (bad key, bad
    model id), as opposed to load or a bad client request."""
    return status in (401, 403, 404)

class FakeUpstream:
    """Records what the gateway sent and answers with a canned response."""

    def __init__(self, status=200, body=None, headers=None, stream=None, raise_exc=None):
        self.status, self.body, self.headers = status, body, headers or LEAKY_HEADERS
        self.stream, self.raise_exc = stream, raise_exc
        self.requests = []

    def handler(self, request):
        self.requests.append(request)
        if self.raise_exc:
            raise self.raise_exc
        if self.stream is not None:
            return httpx.Response(self.status, headers=self.headers, stream=self.stream)
        return httpx.Response(self.status, headers=self.headers, content=self.body)

    def client(self):
        return httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(self.handler))

    @property
    def sent(self):
        return json.loads(self.requests[-1].content)


class SlowStream(httpx.AsyncByteStream):
    """Yields the given chunks, then either raises or hangs; records aclose."""

    def __init__(self, chunks, then=None):
        self.chunks, self.then = chunks, then
        self.closed = False
        self.first_chunk_sent = asyncio.Event()

    async def __aiter__(self):
        for chunk in self.chunks:
            yield chunk
            self.first_chunk_sent.set()
        if self.then is not None:
            raise self.then
        await asyncio.sleep(3600)

    async def aclose(self):
        self.closed = True

"""The credit ledger: lots of credits and what each charged turn took from them.

Balance is the sum of the lots still live, never a stored number, and a lot's
expiry is a comparison at read and charge time, so a lot simply stops counting.
"""
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models


class CreditGrant(models.Model):
    """One lot of credits."""
    PACK = 'pack'
    SUBSCRIPTION = 'subscription'
    SIGNUP = 'signup'
    TRICKLE = 'trickle'
    REWARD = 'reward'
    LAUNCH_BONUS = 'launch_bonus'
    ADJUSTMENT = 'adjustment'
    KINDS = [(k, k) for k in (PACK, SUBSCRIPTION, SIGNUP, TRICKLE, REWARD, LAUNCH_BONUS, ADJUSTMENT)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    kind = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=KINDS)
    credits_granted = models.IntegerField()
    credits_remaining = models.IntegerField()
    expires_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)  # null: never
    basic_only = models.BooleanField(default=False)  # pays basic turns only
    # What makes the lot one of a kind for this person: signup, trickle:<yyyy-mm>,
    # report:<print report id>, and the invoice and subscription refs of billing.
    source_ref = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'source_ref'], name='jusprin_credit_grant_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'expires_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.source_ref}: {self.credits_remaining}/{self.credits_granted}'


class CreditCharge(models.Model):
    """One per charged turn. credits is 0 for a turn covered by unlimited basic
    or a free app turn."""
    BASIC = 'basic'
    EXPERT = 'expert'
    TIERS = [(BASIC, BASIC), (EXPERT, EXPERT)]
    PERSON = 'person'
    APP = 'app'
    ORIGINS = [(PERSON, PERSON), (APP, APP)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    turn_id = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    chat_id = models.CharField(max_length=32, null=True, blank=True)
    alias = models.CharField(max_length=64)
    tier = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=TIERS)
    credits = models.IntegerField()
    origin = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=ORIGINS)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'turn_id'], name='jusprin_credit_charge_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'created_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.turn_id}: {self.credits}'


class CreditAllocation(models.Model):
    """Which lots paid a charge."""
    charge = models.ForeignKey(CreditCharge, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='allocations')
    grant = models.ForeignKey(CreditGrant, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='allocations')
    credits = models.IntegerField()

"""Charging a turn against a person's lots of credits.

The app also starts turns by itself (the file-opened report, the slice-finished
note). Those run on Expert at no credits up to a daily ceiling, then cost what a
basic message costs. Everything else costs the alias's price, except a basic
message on an active Workshop plan, which is free up to the fair-use ceiling.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone as dt_timezone
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from django.db.models import F, Q
from django.utils import timezone

from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .models import CreditAllocation, CreditCharge, CreditGrant


class CreditsExhausted(Exception):
    """The next turn cannot be paid. balance is what can pay this alias, so an
    Expert chat's card never counts the free Standard messages it cannot spend."""

    def __init__(self, balance: int, cost: int, basic_only_credits: int, affordable_aliases: List[str],
                 plan: Optional[str]):
        super().__init__(f'{cost} credits needed, {balance} available')
        self.balance = balance
        self.cost = cost
        self.basic_only_credits = basic_only_credits
        self.affordable_aliases = affordable_aliases
        self.plan = plan

    def details(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            'balance': self.balance,
            'cost': self.cost,
            'basic_only_credits': self.basic_only_credits,
            'affordable_aliases': self.affordable_aliases,
            'plan': self.plan,
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Balance:
    total: int
    basic_only: int

    def payable(self, tier: str) -> int:
        return self.total if tier == CreditCharge.BASIC else self.total - self.basic_only


def _first_of_next_month(now: datetime) -> datetime:
    utc = now.astimezone(dt_timezone.utc)
    year, month = (utc.year + 1, 1) if utc.month == 12 else (utc.year, utc.month + 1)
    return datetime(year, month, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)


def ensure_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime = None) -> None:
    """Creates the lots nobody buys: the first month's, once per account, and
    this month's free Standard messages. Lazy, in place of a monthly sweep over
    every account. Concurrent first requests meet on the unique source_ref."""
    now = now or timezone.now()
    CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref='signup', defaults={
        'kind': CreditGrant.SIGNUP,
        'credits_granted': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': now + timedelta(days=settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_DAYS),
    })
    utc = now.astimezone(dt_timezone.utc)
    CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref=f'trickle:{utc:%Y-%m}', defaults={
        'kind': CreditGrant.TRICKLE,
        'credits_granted': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TRICKLE_CREDITS,
        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TRICKLE_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': _first_of_next_month(now),
        'basic_only': True,
    })


def live_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime):
    """The lots still counting, in draw order: the soonest to expire first,
    never-expiring last, oldest first within one expiry."""
    return (CreditGrant.objects
            .filter(Q(expires_at__isnull=True) | Q(expires_at__gt=now), user_id=user_id)
            .order_by(F('expires_at').asc(nulls_last=True), 'created_at', 'id'))


def balance_of(lots) -> Balance:
    return Balance(total=sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots),
                   basic_only=sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots if lot.basic_only))


def active_v2_plan(user_id: int) -> Optional[JusPrinPlan]:
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=user_id).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS:
        return None
    return plan


def basic_used_this_term(user_id: int, plan: JusPrinPlan, now: datetime) -> int:
    start = plan.current_term_start or now - timedelta(days=30)
    return CreditCharge.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, tier=CreditCharge.BASIC, origin=CreditCharge.PERSON,
                                       created_at__gte=start).count()


def _basic_is_free(user_id: int, plan: Optional[JusPrinPlan], now: datetime) -> bool:
    if plan is None or not settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id].get('unlimited_basic'):
        return False
    return basic_used_this_term(user_id, plan, now) < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_WORKSHOP_BASIC_FAIR_USE


def _price(user_id, alias, origin, plan, now):
    """The tier a turn is charged as, and its credits."""
    if origin == CreditCharge.APP:
        free_today = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, origin=CreditCharge.APP, credits=0,
                                                 created_at__gte=now - timedelta(hours=24)).count()
        if free_today < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_APP_TURNS_PER_DAY:
            return alias.tier, 0
        return CreditCharge.BASIC, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_APP_TURN_CREDITS_PAST_CEILING
    if alias.tier == CreditCharge.BASIC and _basic_is_free(user_id, plan, now):
        return alias.tier, 0
    return alias.tier, alias.credits


def _affordable(balance, aliases, user_id, plan, now) -> List[str]:
    free_basic = _basic_is_free(user_id, plan, now)
    return [alias.id for alias in aliases.values()
            if (free_basic and alias.tier == CreditCharge.BASIC) or balance.payable(alias.tier) >= alias.credits]


def charge_turn(user_id: int, turn_id: str, alias, origin: str, aliases: Dict, chat_id: str = None) -> CreditCharge:
    """Charges a turn once, whatever retries its first request. Raises
    CreditsExhausted with nothing written when the lots cannot pay."""
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user_id, now)
    with transaction.atomic():
        # Holding every live lot, spent ones too, serialises all of a person's
        # charges: this month's free lot always exists, so there is always a row.
        lots = list(live_lots(user_id, now).select_for_update())
        existing = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, turn_id=turn_id).first()
        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        plan = active_v2_plan(user_id)
        tier, cost = _price(user_id, alias, origin, plan, now)
        balance = balance_of(lots)
        if balance.payable(tier) < cost:
            raise CreditsExhausted(balance.payable(tier), cost, balance.basic_only,
                                   _affordable(balance, aliases, user_id, plan, now),
                                   plan.plan_id if plan else None)

        charge = CreditCharge.objects.create(user_id=user_id, turn_id=turn_id, chat_id=chat_id, alias=alias.id,
                                             tier=tier, credits=cost, origin=origin)
        left = cost
        for lot in lots:
            if left == 0:
                break
            if lot.credits_remaining <= 0 or (lot.basic_only and tier != CreditCharge.BASIC):
                continue
            taken = min(left, lot.credits_remaining)
            lot.credits_remaining -= taken

"""What GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account answers: numbers and names only, so the app
can keep reading it for years."""
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Count, Sum
from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone

from app_ent.models import Subscription
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .ledger import active_v2_plan, basic_used_this_term, ensure_lots, live_lots
from .models import CreditCharge, CreditGrant

USAGE_DAYS = 30


def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    lot = {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }
    if grant.basic_only:
        lot['basic_only'] = True
    return lot


def _plan(user, now) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    subscription = Subscription.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    answer = {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': bool(subscription and subscription.active()),
        'auto_reload': False,
    }
    if answer['unlimited_basic']:
        answer['basic_used_this_term'] = basic_used_this_term(user.id, plan, now)
        answer['basic_fair_use'] = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_WORKSHOP_BASIC_FAIR_USE
    return answer


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def _usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    # The gateway never sees a chat's title, so a row names the chat by its id.
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'tier': row['tier'],
                 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or (lot.expires_at is not None and lot.kind != CreditGrant.ADJUSTMENT)]
    return {
        'credits': {'total': sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots), 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': _plan(user, now),
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': _usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
    }

class ConcurrentChargeTests(TransactionTestCase):
    def test_two_turns_cannot_both_spend_the_last_credits_of_one_lot(self):
        user = new_user()
        ensure_lots(user.id)
        CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=user, kind=CreditGrant.SIGNUP).update(credits_remaining=5)
        self.run_at_once(user, ['t1', 't2'])
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes.count('charged'), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes.count('exhausted'), 1)
        self.assertEqual(CreditGrant.objects.get(user=user, kind=CreditGrant.SIGNUP).credits_remaining, 0)
        self.assertEqual(CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user).count(), 1)

    def test_two_first_requests_of_a_new_person_make_one_first_month(self):
        user = new_user()
        self.run_at_once(user, ['t1', 't2'])
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes, ['charged', 'charged'])
        self.assertEqual(CreditGrant.objects.get(user=user, kind=CreditGrant.SIGNUP).credits_remaining, 490)

    def test_one_turn_sent_twice_at_once_pays_once(self):
        user = new_user()
        ensure_lots(user.id)
        self.run_at_once(user, ['same', 'same'])
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes, ['charged', 'charged'])
        self.assertEqual(CreditGrant.objects.get(user=user, kind=CreditGrant.SIGNUP).credits_remaining, 495)

    def run_at_once(self, user, turns):
        barrier = threading.Barrier(len(turns))
        self.outcomes = []

        def run(turn):
            try:
                barrier.wait(timeout=10)
                charge(user, turn)
                self.outcomes.append('charged')
            except CreditsExhausted:
                self.outcomes.append('exhausted')
            finally:
                connection.close()

        threads = [threading.Thread(target=run, args=(turn,)) for turn in turns]
        for thread in threads:
            thread.start()
        for thread in threads:
            thread.join(timeout=30)
        close_old_connections()

9	## Five rules that apply at every point (board 0)
10	
11	1. **One word, one unit, always translated.** "Credits" (decided 2026-11-01), never coins, never tokens. A credit is explained once, in messages: "an Expert message is 5 credits, a Standard message is 1". Every balance is shown translated, "612 credits left. That is 612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", so nobody converts in their head. The Expert count leaves out credits that only Standard can spend: 612 credits of which 50 are free Standard messages is (612 − 50) / 5 = 112, not 122 (the first boards said 122; fixed in canvas version 70). A price never stands alone: "1 credit" confused Kenneth on sight (2026-11-02), so it is always "1 credit a message", "5 credits a message". Dollars appear only on the page where money changes hands. Plans are Hobby ($10 a month), Workshop ($20 a month) and Pay as you go (the never-expiring pack); never Pro, Plus or Premium.
12	2. **Credits only move when the person sends a message.** Turns the app starts (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) are free, and the balance never changes without a message from the person. That one fact is what makes the balance trustworthy; it is stated on the pricing page in one sentence: "Only messages you send cost credits."
13	3. **Expiring credits are named by what they are, with a date. Bought credits are just "credits" and never expire.** "First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec." "Free Standard messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec." "Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire." Never a bare number that mixes them. The draw rule is stated once, in the breakdown: "Expiring credits are used first."
14	4. **Say the number before the boundary, not at it.** Every ceiling (balance, fair use, expiry) is shown on the way there with a count, so reaching it is never news.
15	5. **Nothing typed is lost and nothing stops silently.** A message that cannot be sent stays in the composer. (The earlier draft added "with a way to send it anyway"; the design session dropped the phrase on board 0 because a chat now keeps its model, so there is no way to send. That follows from Kenneth's decision but he has not reviewed the wording. The ways forward are to get more credits or, when free Standard messages remain, to start a Standard chat with the typed text carried over.)
16	
17	## Decisions from the review that shape several points
18	
19	- **The cheap tier is "Standard".** Kenneth, 2026-11-02, in the brainstorm session: not "Basic" (the first boards' word, which sells the tier on being the lesser one) and not "Quick" (my suggestion). Every surface uses it: "Standard · 1 credit a message", "Unlimited Standard messages", "612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", "50 free Standard messages this month", "New Standard chat", and rule 1's explanation. Canvas version 71 says Standard on every board.
20	
21	- **A chat keeps its model.** Kenneth, 2026-11-02, board 3b: for now a person cannot switch the model mid-chat. The model and thinking pickers stay in the composer once a chat has a message, greyed, and hovering either shows a two-line tooltip: "A chat keeps the model and thinking level it started with. Start a new chat to change them." and "Each message you send in this chat costs 5 credits." (board 2c). So there is no "Send with Standard" and no "Switch this chat to Standard" anywhere.
22	- **The app's own turns run on Expert, cost nothing, and do not fix the chat's model.** Kenneth, 2026-11-02, brainstorm session. The turn the app starts when a file opens has to read the plate picture, so it runs on Expert whatever the person would pick; it is free under rule 2; and it does not count as the chat's first message. The person's first message fixes the chat's model, and the greyed pickers follow that message, not the app's note. Without this, every chat that begins with a file would be pinned to Expert before the person could choose, since today the app's note takes the account default and fixes the chat to it.
23	- **A picture in a Standard chat is dropped, and the attachment row says so.** Kenneth, 2026-11-02, brainstorm session: the Standard model cannot see pictures, and he rejected a long clause in the picker option. The notice lives on the staged attachment itself (point 2).
24	- **One action outside the pricing page: "Get more credits".** Kenneth, board 3c: at the moment someone runs out they cannot judge a pack against a plan from a button label, so there is no "Buy" beside "Subscribe" in the app. "Get more credits" opens the pricing page, which explains the difference. The one exception is the savings alert (point 7), whose "Subscribe" names one plan and shows the sums.
25	
26	## The points, in the order a person meets them
27	
28	### 1. First launch: own key or JusPrin account (boards 1a to 1d)
29	
30	Where: the Agent setup in Preferences › Agent (the one setup flow, decided 2026-10-23) and the welcome screen.
31	
32	Kenneth's reaction to the first draft, which put the offer as a small line under "Set up JusPrin": "the most non-obvious way to urge user to sign up". Opinion, as drawn: the offer is the headline on its own surface, "Your first month: 500 credits", with the translation under it, "That is 500 Standard or 100 Expert messages. Your own API key stays free.", and the button names the reward, "Sign in for 500 credits". "Explore first" moves below it. Never "trial" (decided): a trial promises a wall at the end. No dollar figure. The same hierarchy is on the setup row (1a), the welcome screen (1b) and the welcome-back window for a returning v1 user (1c), where signing in is the primary button and Continue secondary. It is "Your own API key", not "your own key" (Kenneth, board 1a).
33	
34	v1 subscribers (Kenneth, board 1c: "make it clear that JusPrin v1 subscribers grandfathered to the $10/mo tier with the original price", "in addition to getting 500 credits"). 1c adds the line "Subscribed to JusPrin v1? You get these 500 credits and keep your original price, on the $10 Hobby plan.", conditional because the app cannot know until sign-in. Board 1d is what that person sees once signed in: "Hobby, at your original $6.99 a month. 750 credits a month: 750 Standard or 150 Expert messages. Plus 500 more for your first month. New subscribers pay $10. You keep this price while subscribed." Nothing to choose, no upgrade prompt; the annual plan reads "at your original $59.99 a year". The design session's fill-ins, not yet confirmed: the price holds "while subscribed"; the 500 stack on the 750 in the first month; and when the move happens (at sign-in or at term end) and how to say that v1 was "unlimited" and Hobby is not are open. v1 has 20 active subscriptions, 15 annual and 5 monthly.
35	
36	### 2. Picking Standard or Expert for a chat (boards 2b, 2c)
37	
38	Where: the model picker in the composer (`ModelPickers.tsx`), chosen before the first message of a chat.
39	
40	Opinion: each option gets the price with its unit and one plain clause about when to use it: "Standard · 1 credit a message · setting up an ordinary print" and "Expert · 5 credits a message · troubleshooting, tricky models, anything you'd ask a person". No model names, no vendor names: the person is choosing how much help to buy, not which company's model. On Standard the price reads "free this month" while free Standard messages last. On the person's own API key there is no price line. After the first message both pickers stay where they are, greyed, with the tooltip from the decision above. The option stays this short: no clause about pictures (Kenneth, 2026-11-02).
41	
42	A picture in a Standard chat (decided 2026-11-02, board 3e on the Compositions page, capture `credits-03e-picture-in-standard-chat.png`): the composer's attachment chip already has a thumbnail, a name line, a second line and a Remove button. In a Standard chat a staged picture keeps its thumbnail, its second line reads "Standard can't see pictures, so this one will not be sent.", and the row gets a "New Expert chat" button beside Remove that starts an Expert chat carrying the typed text and the attachment, the same shape as board 3d's new-chat button. Send stays enabled and the picture is simply left out of the request. One row covers the + menu, drag-and-drop and paste, so the + menu needs no change. As drawn, the two buttons sit on their own line under the sentence, and the sentence is in primary ink rather than grey, since it is a notice and not metadata; it is not in the error colour because Send still works. A Standard chat also lists no picture-returning tools to the model (`view_render` and friends), so the model never calls a tool whose result it cannot read.
43	
44	The turn the app starts when a file opens runs on Expert, free, and leaves the pickers live for the person's first message (decision above). So a chat can hold one Expert turn, the app's, followed by Standard ones; the gateway drops the pictures from that history for the Standard model.
45	
46	Default for a new chat: Expert while the first-month credits last, because the first weeks decide whether the person stays. After that, Standard (board 6a). Whether a later new chat takes the last chosen tier instead is still open. Thinking levels (Fast, Thorough) are drawn at one price per tier; Expert defaults to Thorough and Standard to Fast (the design session's fill-in). Whether Standard shows a thinking picker at all is open; the brainstorm session suggested showing it only on Expert, since Standard has one price anyway.
47	
48	### 3. The balance (boards 2a, 4a to 4c)
49	
50	Where: the composer, and Preferences › Account.
51	
52	Kenneth, on the first draft's sentence-and-lines popover: "Don't reinvent the wheel", and later, with screenshots of Claude's and ChatGPT's usage screens, that both converge on a progress bar per kind of credit. Opinion, as drawn: in the composer only a small ring of what is left, "just like how claude code behaves", with no number beside it and no animation. Hovering or tapping it opens the panel: the total, translated ("612 credits left. That is 612 Standard or 112 Expert messages."), then one bar per kind of credit with what is left and its date, soonest to expire first ("First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec"; "Free Standard messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec"). Every bar's fill is what is left, ChatGPT's way. Bought credits are drawn as a plain number with no bar ("Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire"); Kenneth asked why they get no bar, the design session recommended the plain number because there is no limit to measure against and a "450 of 500" bar would change its 500 on every top-up, and he has not answered, so this is open. What the ring itself measures against is also open (the board uses every credit in the balance when each kind started, a placeholder). One line, "Expiring credits are used first.", then "Get more credits" and "See usage". A person with only their own API key sees no ring.
53	
54	The example balance is 62 first-month + 50 free Standard + 500 bought = 612 (canvas version 70; the first boards had 450 bought beside 112 first-month, which "expiring credits are used first" makes impossible). The usage table shows the purchase as a row, "Bought 500 credits · +500", in the same list as chats and rewards. One gap the example exposed: an unspent 25-credit reward never expires but is not bought, so it has no row in the balance panel and "Bought credits" is the wrong label for it; open for Kenneth.
55	
56	Preferences › Account (4b, 4c) carries the same panel plus: the plan line ("Workshop · $16 a month. Renews 1 Dec."), "Manage plan" and "Get more credits", and Usage in Lovable's shape: a total for the last 30 days, a bar chart per day, and a table of chats with date, chat name, tier, messages and credits, including reward and clawback rows ("Print report · Vent Grille · +25", and a "−25" row with its reason, "Removed: the photo doesn't show a printed object."). "Where did my credits go" has an answer the person can look up alone.
57	
58	### 4. Credits that will expire (boards 2a, 4b)
59	
60	Where: the balance panel and Preferences › Account.
61	
62	First-month credits expire after 30 days, subscription credits at month end, the free Standard allowance at month end. Opinion: the panel always shows the date beside each expiring lot, as a bar. One notice, seven days before a lot expires, inside the composer area once: "388 first-month credits expire on 1 Dec." Never an email for this. When the lot has expired, nothing says "you lost 388 credits"; the panel simply shows what remains. Losing something you did not pay for should not be dramatised.
63	
64	### 5. The next message costs more than the person has (boards 3a to 3d)
65	
66	Where: the composer, before sending; the failed-message card if the gateway refuses anyway.
67	
68	This is the boundary where every surveyed product earns its anger. Opinion, as drawn: catch it before sending. The app knows the balance and the chat's tier, so when the next Expert message cannot be paid, Send is disabled, one line above the composer says why, "You have 3 credits; this Expert chat needs 5 a message.", and the one action is "Get more credits" (3b). The typed text is untouched. Only a race between two sends reaches the gateway's 402; the failed card (3c) then shows the 402's words, "This message needs 5 credits; you have 3.", the same single action, and the message goes back into the composer.
69	
70	"New Standard chat" appears in one case only (3d): the person has free Standard messages left, which can pay for Standard but not for this Expert chat. The line reads "This Expert chat needs 5 credits a message. Your free Standard messages can only pay for Standard." with "Get more credits" and "New Standard chat"; the new chat opens on Standard with the typed text in its box and no earlier messages, so the earlier chat's context is lost (the design session's fill-in; Kenneth has not reviewed 3d, and if he drops New Standard chat altogether the board goes away). Under 5 credits there is no New Standard chat, because, as Kenneth put it, "if a user has <5 credits, no point for new basic chat here": it would run out within a few messages. Bought and plan credits pay for either tier, so only free Standard messages reach this case.
71	
72	Earlier than that (3a): when the balance falls below one session's worth of the chat's tier (about 25 credits for Expert, a placeholder from the four harness sessions of 3 to 6 messages, not from engaged usage), the composer says once "About 5 Expert messages left", so the boundary is expected, not met.

Preferences › Account (4b, 4c) carries the same panel plus: the plan line ("Workshop · $16 a month. Renews 1 Dec."), "Manage plan" and "Get more credits", and Usage in Lovable's shape: a total for the last 30 days, a bar chart per day, and a table of chats with date, chat name, tier, messages and credits, including reward and clawback rows ("Print report · Vent Grille · +25", and a "−25" row with its reason, "Removed: the photo doesn't show a printed object."). "Where did my credits go" has an answer the person can look up alone.

### 4. Credits that will expire (boards 2a, 4b)

Where: the balance panel and Preferences › Account.

First-month credits expire after 30 days, subscription credits at month end, the free Standard allowance at month end. Opinion: the panel always shows the date beside each expiring lot, as a bar. One notice, seven days before a lot expires, inside the composer area once: "388 first-month credits expire on 1 Dec." Never an email for this. When the lot has expired, nothing says "you lost 388 credits"; the panel simply shows what remains. Losing something you did not pay for should not be dramatised.

### 5. The next message costs more than the person has (boards 3a to 3d)

Where: the composer, before sending; the failed-message card if the gateway refuses anyway.

This is the boundary where every surveyed product earns its anger. Opinion, as drawn: catch it before sending. The app knows the balance and the chat's tier, so when the next Expert message cannot be paid, Send is disabled, one line above the composer says why, "You have 3 credits; this Expert chat needs 5 a message.", and the one action is "Get more credits" (3b). The typed text is untouched. Only a race between two sends reaches the gateway's 402; the failed card (3c) then shows the 402's words, "This message needs 5 credits; you have 3.", the same single action, and the message goes back into the composer.

"New Standard chat" appears in one case only (3d): the person has free Standard messages left, which can pay for Standard but not for this Expert chat. The line reads "This Expert chat needs 5 credits a message. Your free Standard messages can only pay for Standard." with "Get more credits" and "New Standard chat"; the new chat opens on Standard with the typed text in its box and no earlier messages, so the earlier chat's context is lost (the design session's fill-in; Kenneth has not reviewed 3d, and if he drops New Standard chat altogether the board goes away). Under 5 credits there is no New Standard chat, because, as Kenneth put it, "if a user has <5 credits, no point for new basic chat here": it would run out within a few messages. Bought and plan credits pay for either tier, so only free Standard messages reach this case.
### 9. When the first month ends (boards 6a, 6b)

Where: the first launch after day 30.

Risk: the person comes back to zero and reads it as "the free trial is over, pay up", the moment Obico's data says people leave. Opinion, as drawn: a new chat starts on Standard and the composer says what is there, "50 free Standard messages this month". No wall, no modal, no notice about what expired, no "upgrade" word. Expert is one click away in the picker (6b) and shows its price. A chat already on Expert stays on Expert, because a chat keeps its model, so opening one shows board 3d.

### 10. Rewards for a print report (boards 8a to 8d)
5:Every "recommend" below is my opinion; every "decided" is Kenneth's. Code facts were read from the checkouts on 2026-11-01 (tsd-enterprise master, JusPrin `jusprin-newui` at 69780c7af4, ops master).
31:"Per user message" divides a whole session's cost, including the turns the app starts by itself (file opened, slice finished), by the messages the person typed. So the margins above already assume app-started turns are not charged (see section 3.3). Two cost prerequisites move these: Anthropic's 5-minute cache expiry during a slow slice rewrote 72k tokens for $0.36 on Opus (section 7.1), and the slicer polling tripled one basic session (section 7.2).
91:Only the first request of a turn charges, as today, so tool-call follow-ups inside a turn are free however many there are. This is what makes "per message" honest and also why the polling fix matters: follow-ups cost the gateway real money while charging nothing.
134:- **Auto-reload with a discount** (decided, optional for the person): a flag on `JusPrinPlan` (`auto_reload`), set from the account page after a first pack purchase so a payment source exists. A Celery task, queued by `charge_turn` when the never-expiring balance drops below 50 credits and the flag is on, creates a Chargebee invoice for add-on `jusprin-500-credits-reload` at $9 (10% off) with `Invoice.create_for_charge_items_and_charges` or the site's equivalent, charged immediately; the `invoice_generated` webhook then grants the lot like any pack. Never charge inside a chat request. A failed payment turns the flag off and tells the person on the account page.
237:1. **Guard in the host** (`ToolExecutionCoordinator`): while a slice the agent started in this turn is running, a `workspace_inspect` that asks for `slicing`, or a `slice_report`, is answered with the tool error code `busy` and the message "The slice is still running. This turn has nothing left to do: the app starts a new turn with the outcome. Finish your reply." After the third such refusal in one turn the host ends the turn (the same path as the person's Stop) and the slice-finished note turn carries on. `busy` is in the one error-code list (`Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`), and a waiting slice is an expected state, so this is normal control flow, not a swallowed error. Each refused call still costs one small request, so three is the cap on the waste.
238:2. **End the turn at `slice_start`** (the real fix, later): when `slice_start` returns `started: true`, the host closes the turn instead of returning the result to the model, and the slice-finished note turn carries both the `tool_result` for that call and the note text in one user message. The model never gets a chance to poll, the person sees the model's text before the tool plus the slice card, and the follow-up request happens once. This touches `ProviderAgent`'s turn continuation and both codecs (a deferred tool result), so it is its own piece of work with the tool-pairing rules of both wire formats tested.
249:- **Review:** `PrintReportReview(report, invalid, note)` with an admin page like `EntPrintShotFeedbackAdmin`, filterable by unreviewed. Marking one invalid writes a `-25` `adjustment` lot (balance can go to zero, not below, for the rest), shown in the Account usage table as a row with the note as its reason ("Removed: the photo doesn't show a printed object.", board 4c), and after two invalid reports the person's reports stop earning. The invalid share is the number to watch; Obico's `PrintShotFeedbackReview.invalid` share can be counted now for a baseline (offered earlier, not yet done).
254:- The sign-up lot is created on first contact (3.5), so no change to the OAuth flow.
262:- Alerts: margin per tier below 20% for three days; free app turns per person above the daily cap; reward invalid share above 10%.

The branch `onboarding-frontend-only` (one commit, `8f4588beae`, 2026-10-06, same on `origin`) adds the first-run path to Home: welcome, import presets from an OrcaSlicer install, confirm or choose a printer, open a project or the bundled example. 174:- **A chat keeps its model** (Kenneth, 2026-11-02, "for now"): the tier is chosen before the person's first message in a chat and never changes after. That is 612 Standard or 122 Expert messages.", then a bar per expiring lot, soonest first, labelled by kind with what is left and its date ("First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec"; "Free Standard messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec"), fill = what is left; never-expiring credits are drawn as a plain number with no bar ("Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire"; Kenneth asked why not a bar and has not answered, decision 13); "Expiring credits are used first."; actions "Get more credits" and "See usage". The bars need each lot's original size, so `lots[]` carries `granted`; a `reward` lot never expires but is not bought, so the panel needs a label for it (no board shows one yet, decision 13); what the ring measures against is open (the board uses the sum of every lot's `granted`, a placeholder). 203:- **Composer: API.** The ring, the hover panel, the picker prices and the pre-send check render inside the composer on every keystroke and must degrade when offline, so they stay on `/account` and `/models`. That API returns numbers and names only, which keeps it cheap to hold backward compatible.
209:- **Offline:** the page shows a plain "can't reach JusPrin" state with a retry, not a browser error; the composer keeps the last `/account` answer.
210:- **Latency:** a remote page takes a visible moment to appear in Preferences › Account; acceptable there, which is one more reason the composer stays on the API.
246:- **Where the button lives** (boards 8a to 8d): the Print history entry gets "Tell us how it printed · 25 credits", the reward named in the button. People come back to Home with the part in hand, so a project card on Home shows the same line when its latest G-code has finished and has no report, and opens Print history filtered to that project; the line goes away after two weeks (a guess at the limit). The one-line G-code marker in a chat keeps its "history" link and gets no button. After sending, the entry's button becomes the row "Report sent · 16:10 · 25 credits added" (8c), since Print history has no composer to show a line in. The record's facts go along automatically: G-code hash, printer, material, process, slice statistics, the plate's manufacturing input hash and, when the person agrees, the project's setup diff from the checkpoint.

## 8. Rewards for print reports

Decided: credits of meaningful value for a photo plus detailed text; this audience did not game Obico's labelling rewards; keep a human review flag.

- **Where the button lives** (boards 8a to 8d): the Print history entry gets "Tell us how it printed · 25 credits", the reward named in the button. People come back to Home with the part in hand, so a project card on Home shows the same line when its latest G-code has finished and has no report, and opens Print history filtered to that project; the line goes away after two weeks (a guess at the limit). The one-line G-code marker in a chat keeps its "history" link and gets no button. The form (8b) opens from the entry and names it ("Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C"), says "A photo of the printed object and a few sentences earn 25 credits.", and takes one or more photos, a text of at least 200 characters (the form says "a few sentences"), and the person's own answer to "How did it come out?" (It worked / Partly / It didn't work), which is the report's outcome, not a print state: Print history stays without a failure state (decided 2026-10-27). After sending, the entry's button becomes the row "Report sent · 16:10 · 25 credits added" (8c), since Print history has no composer to show a line in. The record's facts go along automatically: G-code hash, printer, material, process, slice statistics, the plate's manufacturing input hash and, when the person agrees, the project's setup diff from the checkpoint.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/print_reports` (multipart, bearer token, plain Django on `tsdweb`). Stores a `PrintReport` row and the photos in the object store the way `UploadedTimelapse` stores videos. One report per `(user, gcode_hash)`; at most three rewarded reports a day per person.
- **Reward:** 25 credits (50¢ at pack price, half an expert session) as `CreditGrant(kind=reward, source_ref=report:<id>)`, never expiring, granted at once when the automatic checks pass (photo present and decodable, text length, not a duplicate). The app shows "+25 credits" in the balance.
- **Review:** `PrintReportReview(report, invalid, note)` with an admin page like `EntPrintShotFeedbackAdmin`, filterable by unreviewed. Marking one invalid writes a `-25` `adjustment` lot (balance can go to zero, not below, for the rest), shown in the Account usage table as a row with the note as its reason ("Removed: the photo doesn't show a printed object.", board 4c), and after two invalid reports the person's reports stop earning. The invalid share is the number to watch; Obico's `PrintShotFeedbackReview.invalid` share can be counted now for a baseline (offered earlier, not yet done).
- **Why not in the gateway stream:** reports are not chats; they are the training-data channel, so they get their own table and their own retention rule.

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/print_reports: what earns 25 credits, what does not, and
what a review takes back."""
import io
import json
import uuid
from unittest import mock

from django.contrib.admin.sites import site
from django.test import Client, TestCase
from django.utils import timezone
from datetime import timedelta
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application
from PIL import Image

from app.models import Syndicate, User
from jusprin.ledger.account import account
from jusprin.ledger.ledger import ensure_lots
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditGrant, PrintReport, PrintReportReview
from jusprin.ledger.reports import review_report

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/print_reports'
TEXT = 'The tip of the arrow curled up a little on the first layer, but the rest came out clean. ' * 3


def jpeg(name='part.jpg'):
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new('RGB', (8, 8), 'red').save(buffer, 'JPEG')
    buffer.seek(0)
    buffer.name = name
    return buffer


class PrintReportTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'report-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        application = Application.objects.create(name='JusPrin', client_type='public', authorization_grant_type='authorization-code')
        token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=application, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                           expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1), scope='jusprin')
        self.client = Client(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token.token}')
        storage = mock.patch('jusprin.v2.views.save_file_obj', side_effect=lambda path, *a, **k: (path, f'https://store/{path}'))
        self.stored = storage.start()
        self.addCleanup(storage.stop)

    def report(self, gcode_hash='a71f8c04', text=TEXT, outcome='partly', photos=None, facts=None):
        return self.client.post(URL, {
            'gcode_hash': gcode_hash, 'outcome': outcome, 'text': text,
            'facts': json.dumps(facts if facts is not None else {'project': 'Vent Grille', 'printer': 'Bambu X1C'}),
            'photos': [jpeg()] if photos is None else photos,
        })

    def rewards(self):
        return CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.REWARD)

    def total(self):
        return account(self.user)['credits']['total']


class SubmitTests(PrintReportTestCase):
    def test_a_good_report_earns_25_credits_at_once_that_never_expire(self):
        before = self.total()
        response = self.report()
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['credits'], 25)
        report = PrintReport.objects.get(user=self.user)
        self.assertEqual(report.outcome, 'partly')
        self.assertEqual(report.facts['printer'], 'Bambu X1C')
        self.assertEqual(len(report.photos), 1)
        self.assertTrue(self.stored.called)
        lot = self.rewards().get()
        self.assertEqual(lot.source_ref, f'report:{report.id}')
        self.assertIsNone(lot.expires_at)
        self.assertEqual(self.total(), before + 25)

    def test_it_shows_in_the_activity(self):
        self.report()
        rows = [row for row in account(self.user)['usage_30d']['activity'] if row.get('kind') == 'report']
        self.assertEqual(rows[0]['title'], 'Print report · Vent Grille')
        self.assertEqual(rows[0]['credits'], 25)

    def test_a_second_report_on_the_same_gcode_is_rejected(self):
        self.report()
        self.stored.reset_mock()
        response = self.report()
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 409)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['error']['code'], 'already_reported')
        self.assertFalse(self.stored.called)
        self.assertEqual(self.rewards().count(), 1)

    def test_too_short_a_text_is_rejected(self):
        response = self.report(text='x' * 199)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['error']['code'], 'text_too_short')
        self.assertFalse(PrintReport.objects.exists())

    def test_a_report_needs_a_photo(self):
        self.client.post(URL, {'gcode_hash': 'h', 'outcome': 'worked', 'text': TEXT})
        response = self.client.post(URL, {'gcode_hash': 'h', 'outcome': 'worked', 'text': TEXT})
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['error']['code'], 'photo_needed')

    def test_a_photo_that_cannot_be_decoded_is_rejected(self):
        junk = io.BytesIO(b'not a picture')
        junk.name = 'part.jpg'
        response = self.report(photos=[junk])
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['error']['code'], 'photo_unreadable')
        self.assertFalse(self.stored.called)

    def test_a_bad_outcome_or_no_hash_is_invalid(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.report(outcome='great').status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.report(gcode_hash='').status_code, 400)

    def test_it_takes_a_token(self):
        response = Client().post(URL, {'gcode_hash': 'h', 'outcome': 'worked', 'text': TEXT, 'photos': [jpeg()]})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 401)

    def test_three_reports_earn_in_a_day_and_the_fourth_is_kept_without_earning(self):
        for index in range(3):
            self.assertEqual(self.report(gcode_hash=f'h{index}').json()['credits'], 25)
        response = self.report(gcode_hash='h3')
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['credits'], 0)
        self.assertFalse(PrintReport.objects.get(gcode_hash='h3').rewarded)
        self.assertEqual(self.rewards().count(), 3)


class ReviewTests(PrintReportTestCase):
    def reported(self, gcode_hash='a71f8c04'):
        self.report(gcode_hash=gcode_hash)
        return PrintReport.objects.get(user=self.user, gcode_hash=gcode_hash)

    def test_invalid_takes_the_reward_back_once_and_says_why(self):
        report = self.reported()
        before = self.total()
        note = "Removed: the photo doesn't show a printed object."
        review_report(report, invalid=True, note=note)
        review_report(report, invalid=True, note=note)
        self.assertEqual(self.total(), before - 25)
        adjustment = CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.ADJUSTMENT)
        self.assertEqual(adjustment.credits_granted, -25)
        self.assertEqual(adjustment.credits_remaining, 0)
        rows = [row for row in account(self.user)['usage_30d']['activity'] if row.get('kind') == 'report_removed']
        self.assertEqual(rows, [{'date': rows[0]['date'], 'title': 'Print report · Vent Grille', 'credits': -25,
                                 'kind': 'report_removed', 'note': note}])

    def test_a_spent_reward_comes_out_of_what_else_is_held_down_to_zero_and_not_below(self):
        report = self.reported()
        CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, basic_only=False).update(credits_remaining=0)
        CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, source_ref='signup').update(credits_remaining=10)
        review_report(report, invalid=True, note='Removed.')
        self.assertEqual(CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, source_ref='signup').credits_remaining, 0)
        self.assertFalse(CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, credits_remaining__lt=0).exists())

    def test_free_standard_messages_are_left_alone(self):
        report = self.reported()
        free = CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.TRICKLE).credits_remaining
        CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, basic_only=False).update(credits_remaining=0)
        review_report(report, invalid=True, note='Removed.')
        self.assertEqual(CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.TRICKLE).credits_remaining, free)

    def test_a_valid_review_changes_no_credits(self):
        report = self.reported()
        before = self.total()
        review_report(report, invalid=False)
        self.assertEqual(self.total(), before)

    def test_after_two_invalid_reports_reports_stop_earning(self):
        for name in ('h1', 'h2'):
            review_report(self.reported(name), invalid=True, note='Removed.')
        self.assertEqual(self.report(gcode_hash='h3').json()['credits'], 0)

    def test_the_admin_lists_unreviewed_reports_and_marks_them(self):
        staff = User.objects.create(email='staff@example.com', is_staff=True, is_superuser=True)
        admin_client = Client()
        admin_client.force_login(staff)
        report = self.reported()
        reviewed = self.reported('h2')
        review_report(reviewed, invalid=False)
        listed = admin_client.get('/admin/jusprin/printreport/?reviewed=no')
        self.assertEqual(listed.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(listed.context['cl'].queryset.count(), 1)
        before = self.total()
        response = admin_client.post('/admin/jusprin/printreport/', {'action': 'mark_invalid', '_selected_action': [report.id]})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertTrue(PrintReportReview.objects.get(report=report).invalid)
        self.assertEqual(self.total(), before - 25)
        self.assertIn(PrintReport, site._registry)

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:

  namespace: default
data:

    {"aliases": [{

      "efforts": ["fast", "thorough"], "default_effort": "fast",
      "backends": {
        "anthropic": {

          "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",

          "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_OPENAI_API_KEY",
          "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"}
        }
      },
      "groups": [{"name": "anthropic-main", "format": "anthropic", "percent": 100}]

"""Model aliases for the JusPrin v2 gateway.

The client only ever sees an alias such as "slicer-1". What an alias means
upstream lives in the JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES setting, a JSON env var; nothing
about an upstream model is in code. Upstream keys stay in env vars that the
config names, never in the JSON itself.

Shape (every key shown is required unless marked optional; unknown keys are an
error so a typo fails at startup instead of silently changing routing):

    {
      "aliases": [                         # display order of the models endpoint
        {
          "id": "slicer-1",                # the only model id the client sees
          "label": "Slicer 1",
          "tier": "expert",                # "basic" or "expert"; basic is "Standard" to people
          "credits": 5,                    # what a message costs; efforts cost the same
          "efforts": ["fast", "thorough"], # display order; may be empty
          "default_effort": "fast",        # one of efforts, or null when efforts is empty
          "backends": {                    # keyed by wire format, at least one of:
            "anthropic": {                 #   POST <base_url>/messages, Anthropic Messages API
              "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"},  # must cover every effort
              "headers": {"anthropic-version": "2023-06-01"},     # optional, extra request headers
              "images": true                                      # optional, default true; false strips them
            },
            "responses": {                 #   POST <base_url>/responses, OpenAI Responses API
              "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_OPENAI_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"}
            }
          },
          "groups": [                      # A/B assignment, percents sum to 100
            {"name": "anthropic-main", "format": "anthropic", "percent": 90},
            {"name": "responses-trial", "format": "responses", "percent": 10}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }

A person's group for an alias is fixed by a hash of their user id and the alias
id into one of 100 buckets; groups take consecutive buckets in listed order.
The group decides the "format" the models endpoint reports. It does not decide
where a request goes: the client pins a chat to the format it first saw, so the
endpoint a request arrives on picks the backend.
"""
